p: "וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו ה
'" "And Hashem appeared to him" (Genesis 18:1).
בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה מח
): In Bereishit Rabbah (beginning of Parashah 48): "
וּמִבְּשָׂרִי אֶחֱזֶה אֱלוֹהַּ
" – "'And from my flesh I shall behold God' (Job 19:26) –
אִלּוּלֵי שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי כֵּן, מֵהֵיכָן הָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִגְלֶה עָלַי
? Had I not done so (circumcised myself), from where would the Holy One, blessed be He, have been revealed to me?
וְהוּא תָּמוּהַּ לִכְאוֹרָה
, Now this is seemingly perplexing,
שֶׁהֲרֵי כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר בְּפָרָשַׁת לֶךְ לְךָ שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים "וַיֵּרָא ה' אֶל אַבְרָם" קוֹדֶם הַמִּילָה
. for it was already stated twice in Parashat Lech Lecha, "And Hashem appeared to Abram" prior to the circumcision.
וְאֵין לוֹמַר הַכַּוָּנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִּׁ"י שָׁם (יז, ג) מִפִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
, And one cannot say the intention is as Rashi wrote there (Genesis 17:3) from Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer,
דְּעַד שֶׁלֹּא מָל הָיָה נוֹפֵל עַל פָּנָיו מִמּוֹרָא הַשְּׁכִינָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם
, that before he circumcised himself he would fall upon his face out of dread of the Shechinah, see there,
וְכָאן נֶאֱמַר "וְהוּא יֹשֵׁב
"; whereas here it is stated, "and he was sitting";
דִּלְשׁוֹן הַמִּדְרָשׁ "מֵהֵיכָן הָיָה נִגְלֶה" לֹא מַשְׁמַע כֵּן
. for the wording of the Midrash, "from where would He have been revealed," does not imply this.
וְעוֹד, דְּמִקּוֹדֶם זֶה (יב, ז) לֹא אָמַר שֶׁנָּפַל עַל פָּנָיו
, Furthermore, prior to this (in Genesis 12:7) it did not state that he fell upon his face;
וּמַשְׁמַע דְּאַחַר שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ "וֶהְיֵה תָמִים
", which implies that only after He said to him, "and be whole (tamim)" (17:1),
דְּנוֹדַע לוֹ שֶׁעַתָּה אֵינוֹ תָּמִים
, whereby it became known to him that currently he was not whole,
הָיָה מִתְפַּחֵד לַעֲמוֹד כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵינוֹ תָּמִים וְנָפַל עַל פָּנָיו
; he was afraid to stand so long as he was not whole, and therefore fell upon his face;
אֲבָל מִקּוֹדֶם לֹא יָדַע דְּהָעָרְלָה חִסָּרוֹן
, whereas beforehand he did not know that the foreskin was a deficiency,
לֹא פָּחַד וְלֹא נָפַל עַל פָּנָיו
. so he neither feared nor fell upon his face.
וְאִם כֵּן, הֲרֵי דְּהָיָה נִגְלֶה עָלָיו גַּם מִקּוֹדֶם וְהָיָה יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד
, And if so, behold, He was revealed to him beforehand as well and he was able to stand,
וְגַם הַלָּשׁוֹן "מֵהֵיכָן וְכוּלֵי" צָרִיךְ בֵּיאוּר
. and the phrasing "from where, etc." also requires explanation.

p: וּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה עִיקַּר הַחִילּוּק
, It appears that the primary distinction
דְּשָׁם הָיָה הַהִתְגַּלּוּת לְצוֹרֶךְ דִּבּוּר
, is that there the revelation was for the purpose of a specific divine communication,
וּבָזֶה אֵין צָרִיךְ מִילָה, וְהָיוּ נְבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן
. and for this circumcision is unnecessary, as there were prophets among the nations of the world as well.
וְכָאן נֶאֱמַר "וַיֵּרָא" וְלֹא נִזְכַּר שׁוּם דִּבּוּר אַחֲרָיו לְאֵיזֶה צוֹרֶךְ הָיָה הַהִתְגַּלּוּת
, Whereas here it states, "And He appeared," without mentioning any subsequent speech indicating for what purpose the revelation occurred,
וְעַל כֵּן דָּחֲקוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁהָיָה לְבַקֵּר הַחוֹלֶה
. which is why our Sages of blessed memory were compelled to explain that it was to visit the sick.
אֲבָל פְּשׁוּטוֹ נִרְאֶה דְּעַד הֵנָּה לֹא הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת אֶלָּא לְצוֹרֶךְ דִּבּוּר נְבוּאָה
, However, its plain meaning appears to be that until now there had been no revelation except for the purpose of prophetic speech,
וְהָיָה רַק לִפְרָקִים בְּעֵת שֶׁהֵכִין עַצְמוֹ לְכָךְ
; occurring only intermittently when he prepared himself for it;
אֲבָל עַתָּה נַעֲשָׂה תָּמִים שֶׁגּוּפוֹ מוּכָן תָּמִיד לְכָךְ
, whereas now he became whole, such that his body stood constantly ready for this,
וְזֶהוּ "וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו" – שֶׁעַתָּה נִתְרָאָה אֵלָיו לִהְיוֹת עִמּוֹ תָּמִיד
. and this is the meaning of "And He appeared to him" – that now He manifested Himself to him to remain with him perpetually.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר שָׁם בְּסוֹף פָּרָשַׁת לֶךְ לְךָ גַּבֵּי דִּבּוּר הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמִּילָה
: And this is what is stated there at the end of Parashat Lech Lecha regarding the final communication prior to the circumcision: "
וַיְכַל לְדַבֵּר אִתּוֹ וַיַּעַל אֱלֹהִים מֵעַל אַבְרָהָם" (יז, כב
), "And He finished speaking with him, and God went up from Abraham" (Genesis 17:22),
וְהוּא בִּנְיַן אָב לְכָל הַדִּבּוּרִים הַקּוֹדְמִים
, which establishes a paradigm (binyan av) for all the preceding communications,
שֶׁהָיָה הַהִתְגַּלּוּת רַק בִּשְׁעַת הַדִּבּוּר וְתֵיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ נִסְתַּלֵּק
. namely, that the revelation lasted only during the moment of speech and immediately afterward departed.
רַק שֶׁכָּאן פֵּירֵשׁ הַכָּתוּב זֶה לְבָאֵר הַחִילּוּק שֶׁבֵּין רְאִיָּה שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמִּילָה לִרְאִיָּה שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ
, Only here did Scripture state this explicitly in order to clarify the distinction between the vision before circumcision and the vision after it:
דְּשָׁם לֹא הָיָה לְצוֹרֶךְ דִּבּוּר אוֹ שׁוּם צוֹרֶךְ, וְלֹא נִסְתַּלֵּק כְּלָל
, for there (after circumcision) it was not for the sake of a specific communication or any external need, and He did not depart at all,
כִּי כְּבָר נִתְקַדֵּשׁ גּוּפוֹ לִהְיוֹת דִּירָה לַשְּׁכִינָה בְּלִבּוֹ תָּמִיד
, because his physical body had already been sanctified to serve as a permanent dwelling place for the Shechinah within his heart,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה עַל פָּסוּק "וְלִבִּי עֵר
" just as it is among the children of Israel, as they taught in Shir HaShirim Rabbah on the verse "and my heart is awake" (Song of Songs 5:2):
מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי וְגוֹמֵר
". From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel? As it is stated: "The rock of my heart, etc." (Psalms 73:26).

p: וּבְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת בְּיִחוּד אִיתָא (בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן מח
): And regarding the Sabbath day in particular, it is stated (in Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48): "'
וְשָׁמְרוּ וְגוֹמֵר' – תְּרֵין זִמְנִין וְכוּלֵי, שַׁבָּת לָקֳבֵל שְׁכִינְתָּא עִלָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה וְכוּלֵי
, "'And the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath...' – mentioned twice, etc., Shabbat corresponds to the Upper Shechinah and the Lower Shechinah, etc.,
זַכָּאָה אִיהוּ מַאן דְּעָבִיד לוֹן דִּירָה בְּשַׁבָּת בִּתְרֵי בָּתֵּי לִבָּא וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. praiseworthy is he who makes for them a dwelling place on Shabbat within the two chambers of the heart, etc.," see there.
וּבְתִיקּוּן ו' דְּבִזְמַנָּא דִּשְׁכִינְתָּא בְּגָלוּתָא אִתְּמַר בַּהּ (בִּשְׁכִינְתָּא עִלָּאָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם דַּעֲלַהּ קָאֵי) וְכוּלֵי
, And in Tikkun 6: that during the time when the Shechinah is in exile, it is said of Her (of the Upper Shechinah, see there that it refers to Her), etc.,
אֶלָּא בְּשַׁבָּת וְיוֹם טוֹב וְכוּלֵי, וְכַמָּה נְפָשׁוֹת יְתֵירִין קָא נָחְתִין עִמַּהּ לְדַיְירָא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
, except on Shabbat and Yom Tov, etc., when numerosos additional souls (neshamot yeteirot) descend with Her to dwell within Israel;
הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב "וְשָׁמְרוּ וְגוֹמֵר לְדֹרֹתָם" – זַכָּאָה אִיהוּ מַאן דִּמְתַקֵּן לַהּ דִּירָה נָאָה בְּלִבֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם

. thus it is written, "And they shall keep the Sabbath... throughout their generations (ledorotam)" – praiseworthy is he who prepares for Her a beautiful dwelling (dirah) in his heart, etc., see there.
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם תִּיקּוּן כ"ד: "שְׁכִינְתָּא דְּאִיהִי נְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה
", And see there, Tikkun 24: "The Shechinah, who is the additional soul (neshamah yeteirah),"
וְשָׁם תִּיקּוּן מ"ז אִיתָא: "שַׁבָּת שְׁכִינְתָּא
". and there in Tikkun 47 it is stated: "Shabbat is the Shechinah."
וְהַיְינוּ דִּנְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת
, This means that the additional soul is itself called "Shabbat,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (יִתְרוֹ פח עַמּוּד ב
): just as is written in the Zohar (Yitro 88b): "
בְּשַׁבַּתָּא יָהֲבִין לֵיהּ לְבַר נָשׁ נִשְׁמְתָא וְכוּלֵי, וּבְגִין כָּךְ אִקְרֵי שַׁבָּת
", "On Shabbat they grant a person a supernal soul, etc., and on account of this it is called Shabbat,"
וְעַיֵּין עוֹד שָׁם: "מַהוּ שַׁבָּת? שְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵי
", and see further there: "What is Shabbat? The Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, etc.,"
הַיְינוּ דְּ"חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ" (דְּבָרִים לב, ט
). meaning that "Hashem's portion is His people" (Deuteronomy 32:9).
וּכְמוֹ כָּל נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה
, And just as all the souls of Israel derive from the letters of the Torah,
וְאוֹרַיְיתָא כֻּלַּהּ שְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר בְּכַמָּה דּוּכְתֵּי
, and the entire Torah is the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, as is written in the Zohar in several places,
וְשַׁבָּת כְּלָלָא דְּכָל אוֹרַיְיתָא הוּא גַּם כֵּן שְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
, so too Shabbat, which is the totality of the entire Torah, is likewise the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He,
וְהַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה בְּשֵׁם זֶה
. and the additional soul bears this very name.

p: וְכִדְמַשְׁמַע מִלְּשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיח סוֹף עַמּוּד א וְרֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב
): And as is implied by the phrasing of the Gemara (Shabbat 118a end and 118b beginning): "
כָּל הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת", וְלֹא "הַמִּתְעַנֵּג בְּשַׁבָּת
" "Whoever delights the Shabbat (ha-me'aneg et ha-Shabbat)," rather than "whoever delights himself on Shabbat (ha-mit'aneg be-Shabbat)" (
וּמִיהוּ בָּרִי"ף שָׁם הַגִּירְסָא בַּמֵּימְרָא הָרִאשׁוֹנָה: "כָּל מִי שֶׁמְּעַנֵּג עַצְמוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת
", (although in the Rif there, the text in the first statement reads: "Whoever delights himself on Shabbat,"
וּבַשְּׁאִילְתּוֹת רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית הַגִּירְסָא בְּמֵימְרָא שְׁנִיָּה: "הַמִּתְעַנֵּג בְּשַׁבָּת
", and in the She'iltot at the beginning of Parashat Bereishit, the text in the second statement reads: "Whoever delights himself on Shabbat,"
אֲבָל לֹא מָצָאנוּ חָבֵר לְנוּסְחָאוֹת אֵלּוּ
), yet we have found no corroborating support for these variant readings),
וְעַל הַיּוֹם לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ עוֹנֶג, אֲבָל הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה הִיא נֶהֱנֵית מֵעִנּוּגֵי שַׁבָּת
, for the concept of experiencing delight does not apply to the temporal day itself; rather, it is the additional soul that derives pleasure from the delights of Shabbat,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִּׁ"י (תַּעֲנִית כז: וּבֵיצָה טז.) דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל נְשָׁמָה
. just as Rashi wrote (Ta'anit 27b and Beitzah 16a, s.v. Neshamah).
וְכֵן מַשְׁמַע בַּזֹּהַר (יִתְרוֹ פח עַמּוּד ב
): And so it is implied in the Zohar (Yitro 88b): "
בְּשַׁבַּתָּא יָהֲבִין לֵיהּ לְבַר נָשׁ נִשְׁמְתָא אַחֲרָא עִלָּאָה, נִשְׁמְתָא דְּכָל שְׁלִימוּ בַּהּ כְּדוּגְמָא דְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי
, "On Shabbat they grant a person another, supernal soul, a soul in which all perfection resides, after the pattern of the World to Come,
וּבְגִין כָּךְ אִקְרֵי שַׁבָּת. מַהוּ שַׁבָּת? שְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, שְׁמָא דְּאִיהוּ שְׁלִים וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. and therefore it is called Shabbat. What is Shabbat? The Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, the Name that is complete, etc.," see there.
מַשְׁמַע לְפִי שֶׁהוּא דּוּגְמָא דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא עַל כֵּן נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת
, This implies that because it is a reflection of the World to Come, it is therefore called Shabbat;
דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא נִקְרָא "יוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת" בַּמִּשְׁנָה (סוֹף תָּמִיד) וּבַגְּמָרָא (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לא
.). for the World to Come is called "a day that is entirely Shabbat" in the Mishnah (end of Tamid) and in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 31a).
וְעַל שַׁבָּת אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נז:) דְּהוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא וְאֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בּוֹ
. And regarding Shabbat they said (Berakhot 57b) that it is a semblance of the World to Come and one-sixtieth thereof.
וְהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ (שָׁם יז עַמּוּד א) דְּאֵין בּוֹ וְכוּלֵי אֶלָּא וְכוּלֵי וְנֶהֱנִין מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיֶּחֱזוּ אֶת וְגוֹמֵר

". Now concerning the World to Come, they stated (Berakhot 17a) that there is neither eating nor drinking in it, etc., rather the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads and delight in the radiance of the Shechinah, as it is stated: "And they beheld God, etc." (Exodus 24:11).
וְעַל כֵּן בְּשַׁבָּת גַּם כֵּן מֵעֵין זֶה
, Consequently, on Shabbat there is likewise a foretaste of this,
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה שֶׁהוּא כְּדוּגְמָא דִּידֵיהּ
and this occurs specifically through the additional soul, which is after its pattern (
וּבְפָרָשַׁת אֱמוֹר צה עַמּוּד א אִיתָא הַלָּשׁוֹן "כְּגַוְונָא וְכוּלֵי
"). (and in Zohar Parashat Emor 95a, the phrasing is "like the manner of, etc.").

p: וּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר "שְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא", הַיְינוּ כִּי נֶפֶשׁ רוּחַ נְשָׁמָה דְּשַׁבָּת מֵאֲצִילוּת
, And what it stated, that it is "the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He," is because the Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah of Shabbat stem from the realm of Atzilut (Emanation),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר (תִּיקּוּן ו
), as is written in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 6),
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם דְּנִשְׁמָתִין מִסִּטְרָא דִּשְׁכִינְתָּא עִלָּאָה וְנַפְשִׁין מִסִּטְרָא דִּשְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה, וְיַעֲשֶׂה שָׁם בְּעִיּוּן
. and see there well that the neshamot emanate from the side of the Upper Shechinah and the nefashot emanate from the side of the Lower Shechinah.
וְזֶהוּ "שַׁבָּת עִלָּאָה" הַנִּזְכָּר בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (יִתְרוֹ צב עַמּוּד א וּבְפָרָשַׁת תְּרוּמָה קלח עַמּוּד א) דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל מִזְמוֹר, עַיֵּין שָׁם
, And this is the "Upper Shabbat" mentioned in Ra'aya Meheimna (Yitro 92a and Parashat Terumah 138a, s.v. Mizmor), see there, (
וּבְפָרָשַׁת פִּנְחָס רנז סוֹף עַמּוּד א) דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל פִּקּוּדָא עֲשִׂירָאָה
: (and in Parashat Pinchas 257a end, s.v. Pikuda Asira'ah): "
שְׁכִינְתָּא אִתְקְרִיאַת שַׁבָּת מִסִּטְרָא וְכוּלֵי, מִבִּינָה וּלְעֵילָא אִיהִי מְנוּחָה וְעוֹנֶג וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. "The Shechinah is called Shabbat from the side of, etc., from Binah and above She is rest and delight, etc.," see there.
וּבִינָה הוּא שַׁבָּת וּשְׁכִינְתָּא עִלָּאָה
, Thus Binah is Shabbat and the Upper Shechinah,
וּבְתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר (תִּיקּוּן יט): "שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל – בִּינָה, שַׁבָּת הַקָּטָן – מַלְכוּת", עַיֵּין שָׁם, וְהַיְינוּ עִלָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה
. and in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 19): "The Great Shabbat is Binah; the Small Shabbat is Malchut," see there, which corresponds to the Upper and the Lower.
וְכֵן "תְּרֵי בָּתֵּי לִבָּא" הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אִיתָא (שָׁם בְּתִיקּוּן כב
): Similarly, regarding the "two chambers of the heart" mentioned above, it is stated (there in Tikkun 22): "
הֵ"א עִלָּאָה הֵ"א תַּתָּאָה בִּתְרֵי בָּתֵּי לִבָּא, דְּאִינּוּן לָקֳבֵל בַּיִת רִאשׁוֹן וּבַיִת שֵׁנִי", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. "The upper Hei and the lower Hei reside in the two chambers of the heart, corresponding to the First Temple and the Second Temple," see there.
וְשָׁם רֵישׁ תִּיקּוּן נ"ח: "תְּרֵי בָּתֵּי לִבָּא אִינּוּן תְּרֵי בִּנְיָנִין וְכוּלֵי דְּאִמָּא עִלָּאָה וְתִנְיָנָא דְּאִמָּא תַּתָּאָה", עַיֵּין שָׁם
And there at the beginning of Tikkun 58: "The two chambers of the heart are two edifices, etc., of the Upper Mother (Imma Ila'ah) and the second of the Lower Mother (Imma Tata'ah)," see there (
וְהֵם הַשְּׁנַיִם דְּ"לֵב חָכָם" וְ"לֵב כְּסִיל" הַנִּזְכָּר בַּכָּתוּב
, (and they correspond to the two aspects of "the heart of the wise" and "the heart of the fool" mentioned in Scripture Ecclesiastes 10:2,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתִיקּוּן ס"ט דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל קָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, עַיֵּין שָׁם
, as is written in Tikkun 69, s.v. Kam Rabbi Shimon, see there;
וּמִסְּתָמָא מַלְכוּת לִשְׂמֹאל דְּשָׁם מִשְׁכַּן יֵצֶר הָרָע, דְּ"רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת וְכוּלֵי" כַּיָּדוּעַ
), and presumably Malchut is positioned to the left, where the abode of the evil inclination lies, for "her feet go down to death" Proverbs 5:5, as is known),
וּבַאֲצִילוּת "אִיהוּ וְחַיּוֹהִי חַד וְכוּלֵי", וְהַכֹּל שְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
. and within the world of Atzilut, "He and His life-forces are entirely One, etc.," and everything is the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He.

h: The Zohar on the Rising Shechinah

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayakhel 13:179-182: “Come and see: there are days and there are days. The ordinary days, as stated, stand outside for the nations. The days of Shabbos, which are the days of the week, stand for Israel. When this point rises, everything is concealed, and it rises; once it rises, it is called Shabbos. What is Shabbos? If you say it is because of cessation, as it is written, “For on it He ceased,” that is correct. But the mystery of the matter is this: once this point rises and light shines, it is crowned with the patriarchs. paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayakhel 14:186-187: “A mystery of mysteries for those who know wisdom: fortunate are they when this spirit is aroused. This spirit is an extension of this point; it issues from it and spreads through the world. That is the mystery of Shabbos that rests below. Therefore keeping is written concerning it: “The Children of Israel shall keep Shabbos.” As explained, it does not say merely “Shabbos,” but “es haShabbos,” to include that spirit which rests upon all. It must be guarded, since it abides with a person; therefore it is written, “Everyone who keeps Shabbos from profaning it.” Within this mystery is another mystery. This spirit enjoys, on this day, Israel’s pleasures and their delight. Therefore one must give it delight through eating and drinking three times, in the three meals of the three levels of faith, as explained. It receives joy and delight through those meals of Israel. Fortunate is the portion of one who gives it pleasure and delights it on this day.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: רָזָא דְּרָזִין לְיַדְעֵי חָכְמְתָא, זַכָּאִין אִינּוּן כַּד הַאי רוּחָא אִתְעָר. הַאי רוּחָא אִיהוּ אִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתָא דְּהַאי נְקוּדָה, וְנָפְקָא מִינָּהּ, וְאִתְפַּשְּׁטָא בְּעָלְמָא, וְהַהוּא הֲוֵי רָזָא דְּשַׁבָּת, דְּשָׁרָא לְתַתָּא, וְעַל דָּא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ שְׁמִירָה, (שמות ל״א:ט״ז) וְשָׁמְרוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת, וְהָא אוּקְמוּהָ, שַׁבָּת לָא כְּתִיב, אֶלָּא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת, לְאַסְגָּאָה הַהוּא רוּחָא דְּשָׁרֵי עַל כֹּלָּא, וְאִצְטְרִיךְ לְנַטְרָא לֵיהּ, הוֹאִיל וְקַיְּימָא עִמֵּיהּ דְּבַר נָשׁ, וְעַל דָּא כְּתִיב, (ישעיהו נ״ו:ו׳) כָּל שׁוֹמֵר שַׁבָּת מֵחַלְּלוֹ. בְּהַאי רָזָא אִית רָזָא אַחֲרָא. הַאי רוּחָא, אִתְהֲנִי בְּהַאי יוֹמָא, מֵהֲנָאוֹתָן דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמֵעִנּוּגָא דִּלְהוֹן, וּבְגִין דָּא, בָּעֵי לְמֵיהַב לֵיהּ עִנּוּגָא, בְּמֵיכְלָא וּבְמִשְׁתְּיָא, תְּלָת זִמְנִין, בִּתְלַת סְעוּדָתִין, דִּתְלַת דַּרְגֵּי מְהֵימְנוּתָא, כְּמָה דְּאוּקְמוּהָ. וְהַאי נָטִיל חֶדְוָה וְעִנּוּגָא, בְּאִינּוּן סְעוּדָתֵי דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל. זַכָּאָה חוּלָקֵיהּ, מַאן דְּאַהֲנֵי לֵיהּ, וּמְעַנֵג לֵיהּ, בְּהַאי יוֹמָא.

It was, however, a precious gift in His treasury, which He concealed from the wicked so that they would not benefit from this sanctity, and gave to Israel. Concerning this it says, “To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you,” as our Sages said in Shabbos 10b. This is the sanctity from Above with which the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctifies a person of Israel on Shabbos: he merits an additional soul through the flow of sanctity from Above, according to how fully he has become a prepared vessel through the two preceding forms of sanctity from below, as explained.”

p: הִנֵּה מְבוֹאָר דְּהַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה הִיא מֵהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת נְהוֹרָא דִּשְׁכִינְתָּא שֶׁנִּקְרָא שַׁבָּת
. Behold, it is clearly explained that the additional soul stems from the expansion of the light of the Shechinah, which is called Shabbat.
וְשָׁם רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב אָמַר
: And there at the top of 204b it states: "
הַאי רוּחָא (רָצָה לוֹמַר הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה) אִיהוּ אִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתָא דְּהַאי נְקוּדָה וְכוּלֵי
, "This spirit (meaning the additional soul) is the expansion of this supernal point, etc., '
אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת' – לְאַסְגָּאָה הַהוּא רוּחָא וְכוּלֵי, הַאי רוּחָא אִתְהֲנֵי וְכוּלֵי
, 'et ha-Shabbat' comes to include and amplify that spirit, etc., this spirit derives pleasure, etc.,
זַכָּאָה מַאן דְּאַהֲנֵי לֵיהּ וּמְעַנֵּג לֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי", יְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּעִיּוּן
. praiseworthy is he who benefits it and delights it, etc.," examine it there well.
וּמְפוֹרָשׁ כָּאן דְּהָעִנּוּגִין הוּא לְהַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה, וּדְהִיא נִקְרָא "אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
" Thus it is explicitly stated here that the delights of Shabbat are for the additional soul, and that this soul itself is called "et ha-Shabbat" (
דְּבְכָל מָקוֹם "אֶת" מְרַבֵּי הַטָּפֵל, כְּמוֹ "אֶת בְּשָׂרוֹ" גַּבֵּי טְבִילָה מְרַבִּינַן שְׂעָרוֹ הַטָּפֵל לִבְשָׂרוֹ

, (for throughout the Talmud, the word "et" comes to include that which is secondary and attached tafel, just as from "et besaro" his flesh regarding ritual immersion we include his hair, which is subordinate to his flesh,
וְגַבֵּי שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל מְרַבִּינַן עוֹרוֹ, וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם
. and regarding the ox condemned to stoning we include its hide, and similarly everywhere.
וְכֵן הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה, אַף דְּהִיא מֵאוֹר הַשְּׁכִינָה הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט
, So too regarding the additional soul: even though it emanates from the expanding light of the Shechinah,
עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים ח עַמּוּד א: "צַדִּיקִים בִּפְנֵי שְׁכִינָה כְּנֵר בִּפְנֵי הָאבוּקָה
", concerning this they stated in Pesachim 8a: "The righteous before the Shechinah are like a candle before a torch,"
וְאוֹר הַנֵּר הוּא מֵאוֹר הָאבוּקָה
, and the flame of the candle isKindled from the flame of the torch,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ", וְנֶאֱמַר: "וַיִּפַּח בְּאַפָּיו וְגוֹמֵר" – מַאן דְּנָפַח מִתּוֹכוֹ נָפַח
, as it is written: "For Hashem's portion is His people," and it is stated: "And He blew into his nostrils, etc." (Genesis 2:7) – one who blows, blows from within himself;
אֲבָל הוּא נֶחְשָׁב טָפֵל לְגַבֵּי הָעִיקָּר
). yet it is nevertheless considered secondary tafel in relation to the primary Source).
וּמְדֻיָּק לְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא "הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת" עַל הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה דְּנִקְרָא "אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
", Hence the wording of the Gemara, "He who delights et ha-Shabbat," is exact, referring to the additional soul which is termed "et ha-Shabbat,"
וְזֶהוּ הַדִּירָה דִּשְׁכִינְתָּא בְּלִבֵּיהּ וּשְׁנֵי בָּתֵּי לִבָּא
. and this constitutes the dwelling of the Shechinah within his heart and the two chambers of the heart.

p: כִּי גַּם שְׁכִינָה תַּתָּאָה דְּהִיא מַלְכוּת, שֶׁמִּזֶּה בָּא הַיִּרְאָה כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
, For the Lower Shechinah as well, which is Malchut—from which stems awe, like one standing before the King, as mentioned above—
וְהִיא הָאִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה', שֶׁהִיא הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל דִּנְפָשׁוֹת בִּצְרוֹר הַחַיִּים
, is the "woman who fears Hashem" (Proverbs 31:30), namely Knesset Yisrael (the Ecclesia of Israel), wherein all souls are bound in the bundle of life,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְהָיְתָה נֶפֶשׁ אֲדֹנִי צְרוּרָה בִּצְרוֹר הַחַיִּים אֵת ה'" (שְׁמוּאֵל א כה, כט
), as it is written: "And the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with (et) Hashem" (I Samuel 25:29),
דְּהַיְינוּ בְּמִדָּה זוֹ שֶׁנִּקְרָא "אֵת ה'" – טָפֵל לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה
. referring to this attribute which is called "et Hashem," subordinate and joined to the Tetragrammaton.
וּבְסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר סִימָן כ"ט
: And in Sefer HaBahir, section 29: "
מַאי 'וַיִּנָּפַשׁ'? מְלַמֵּד שֶׁיּוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת מְקַיֵּים כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת
. "What is the meaning of 'and He was refreshed (vayinafash)' (Exodus 31:17)? It teaches that the Sabbath day sustains all souls.
דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁמִּשָּׁם פּוֹרְחִים כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. Another interpretation: that from there all souls fly forth, etc.," see there.
וְשֶׁמְּקַיֵּים הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה דְּשַׁבָּת
, And that it "sustains" them is through the additional soul of Shabbat:
אַף שֶׁנִּסְתַּלֶּקֶת אַחַר כָּךְ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם רְשִׁימוּ נִשְׁאָר
, for even though it departs after Shabbat, nevertheless a spiritual imprint (reshimu) remains behind,
כַּיָּדוּעַ בְּכָל דְּבַר קְדוּשָּׁה דְּמַשְׁאִיר רְשִׁימוּ
, as is known regarding every matter of holiness that it leaves a lasting trace,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ"י עַל שַׁבָּת בְּיִחוּד
. and as the Ari wrote regarding Shabbat in particular.
וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּמְּכִילְתָּא (פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּסַּע רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה ה
) And so it is found in the Mekhilta (Parashat Beshalach, Parashat Vayassa, beginning of chapter 5),
שֶׁכָּל הַמְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת מְרוּחָק מִן הָעֲבֵירָה, מִקְּרָא: "וְשֹׁמֵר יָדוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע" (יְשַׁעְיָה נו, ב
). that whoever observes Shabbat is distanced from transgression, derived from the verse: "Who keeps Shabbat from profaning it, and keeps his hand from doing any evil" (Isaiah 56:2).
וּמִזֶּה הוּא מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים רֵישׁ שַׁעַר הַשַּׁבָּת
, And from this stems what is written in Pri Etz Chaim at the beginning of Sha'ar HaShabbat,
דְּנִיצּוֹל מִקִּטְרוּג הַיֵּצֶר כָּל יְמֵי הַשָּׁבוּעַ, וְזֶהוּ קִיּוּם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת
. that one is protected from the incitement of the evil inclination throughout all the days of the week; and this is the sustaining of the souls.

p: וּ"מִשָּׁם גַּם כֵּן פּוֹרְחִין כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת", הַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְחַלְּקוּ נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
, And "from there all souls fly forth" refers to the state after the souls of Israel were set apart,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה.) אַהָא דְּ"נְשָׁמוֹת שֶׁבַּגּוּף
", as Tosafot wrote (Avodah Zarah 5a) on the statement "until all the souls in the Guf (heavenly treasury) are finished,"
דְּנַפְשׁוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הֵם מֵאוֹצָר וְגוּף אַחֵר
, that the souls of idolaters derive from a different treasury and chamber,
וּמֵבִיא הַחִידָ"א דְּזֶהוּ אַחַר שֶׁנִּבְחֲרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
. and the Chida cites that this distinction took effect after Israel was chosen.
וּמִדָּה זוֹ הָאַחֲרוֹנָה נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן "גּוּף", שֶׁהִיא כְּגוּף לְגַבֵּי הַנְּשָׁמָה
, And this final attribute (Malchut) is also called "Guf" (Body), as it is like a body in relation to the soul (Binah / Ze'ir Anpin),
כִּי זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין וְנוּקְבָא הֵם נְשָׁמָה וְגוּף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם עַל אַבְרָהָם וְשָׂרָה
, for Ze'ir Anpin and Nukva are soul and body, as is written in Midrash HaNe'elam regarding Abraham and Sarah,
וְאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת כד.): "אִשְׁתּוֹ כְּגוּפוֹ", וְעַיֵּין מְאוֹרֵי אוֹר מַעֲרֶכֶת א' אוֹת ל"ח
. and our Sages said (Berakhot 24a): "A man's wife is like his own body," and see Me'orei Ohr, Ma'arekhet Alef, section 38.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דִּדְמַאי דַּאֲפִילּוּ עַם הָאָרֶץ אֵימַת הַשַּׁבָּת עָלָיו
, And therefore they stated in the Yerushalmi Demai that even upon an unlearned person (am ha'aretz) the awe of Shabbat rests,
וּבְתַעֲנִית (ח:) דְּ"יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי" נִקְרְאוּ שׁוֹמְרֵי שַׁבָּת, עַיֵּין שָׁם
. and in Ta'anit (8b) that "those who fear My Name" (Malachi 3:20) refers to those who observe Shabbat, see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּשַׁבָּת שְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, דְּאָז הִתְגַּלּוּת כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ
, And this is because Shabbat is the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, for then occurs the revelation of the glory of His kingship,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי נִתְעַלָּה וְיָשַׁב עַל כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדוֹ
", as we say in the liturgy: "On the seventh day He elevated Himself and sat upon His Throne of Glory,"
וּמִזֶּה נוֹפֵל הַיִּרְאָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
. and from this revelation awe descends upon man, as mentioned above.

p: וְהַיִּרְאָה הוּא גַּם כֵּן בַּלֵּב, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּיוֹמָא עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "לָמָּה זֶּה מְחִיר בְּיַד כְּסִיל לִקְנוֹת חָכְמָה וְלֵב אָיִן

" – And fear of Heaven likewise resides in the heart, as they taught (in Yoma 72b) on the verse "Why is there a purchase price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when there is no heart?" (Proverbs 17:16) –
כְּשֶׁאֵין בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם דְּזֶה כְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ לֵב כְּלָל
. that when a person lacks fear of Heaven, it is as though he has no heart at all.
וְעַל יְדֵי יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם מִסְתַּלֵּק הַכְּסִילוּת דְּ"לֵב כְּסִיל" שֶׁמִּלִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ
, And through fear of Heaven, the folly of the "heart of the fool" on his left side departs,
וּ"בִינָה לִבָּא" הוּא כְּשֶׁנִּתּוֹסֵף חָכְמָה וּבִינָה בְּהַ"לֵּב חָכָם" לִימִינוֹ
, while "Binah is the heart" manifests when wisdom and understanding are increased within the "heart of the wise" on his right side;
דְּהַחָכְמָה בַּלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּבְלֵב כָּל חֲכַם לֵב נָתַתִּי חָכְמָה" (שְׁמוֹת לא, ו) וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ מִשְׁלֵי
, for wisdom settles in the heart, as it is written: "And in the heart of all who are wise-hearted I have placed wisdom" (Exodus 31:6), and as written in Midrash Mishlei,
וְאָז יִתּוֹסֵף עַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ הַכָּרָה יְתֵירָה
. and then fear of Heaven is further elevated when accompanied by heightened cognitive recognition.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "לְהַקְשִׁיב לַחָכְמָה אָזְנֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר כִּי אִם לַבִּינָה תִקְרָא וְגוֹמֵר אָז תָּבִין יִרְאַת ה' וְדַעַת אֱלֹהִים תִּמְצָא" (מִשְׁלֵי ב, ב-ה
), As it is written: "To incline your ear to wisdom... if you call out for understanding... then you will understand the fear of Hashem, and find the knowledge (Da'at) of God" (Proverbs 2:2-5),
הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּמְצָא דַּעַת אֱלֹהִים בְּיוֹתֵר
meaning that through finding the knowledge (Da'at) of God in greater measure (
כִּי דַּעַת הוּא חִבּוּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה כַּיָּדוּעַ, וְהַיְינוּ חִבּוּר מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא
, (for Da'at is the union of Chokhmah and Binah, as is known, which is the integration of the mind and the heart:
דְּבַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ יוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג הַרְבֵּה
, for through the wisdom in the brain one can intellectually grasp much,
וּכְשֶׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ בְּאוּבְנְתָא דְּלִבָּא כְּפִי הֲבָנָתוֹ בְּחָכְמָה, זֶהוּ דַּעַת
, and when he internalizes and feels within the comprehension of his heart commensurate with his intellectual grasp in Chokhmah, that constitutes Da'at,
שֶׁהוּא פְּנִימִיּוּת הַכֶּתֶר שֶׁבַּחִיצוֹנִיּוּת כַּיָּדוּעַ
, which is the inner dimension of Keter as enclothed within the lower faculties, as is known;
וְעַל פִּי פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא דַּעַת הוּא רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵחָכְמָה וְהַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׂכֶל
), and based on Parashat Ki Tisa, Da'at is the Holy Spirit Ruach HaKodesh, namely that which transcends mere wisdom and rational intellect),
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יַגִּיעַ לְבִינָה בְּיִרְאַת ה
', through this one arrives at true understanding (Binah) in the fear of Hashem,
וּכְמוֹ הַמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁזָּעִים וְחָלִים מִפַּחְדּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, מַה שֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָשָׂר וָדָם לְהַגִּיעַ לְיִרְאָה זוֹ

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 22:13: ““Cain departed [vayetze] from the presence of the Lord, and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden” (Genesis 4:16). “Cain departed from the presence of the Lord” – from where did he depart? Rabbi Yudan said in the name of Rabbi Aivu: He cast the words behind him and departed, as though deceiving the Most High. Rabbi Berekhya said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Shimon: He departed as one who shows a split hoof, and as one who deceives his Creator. Rabbi Ḥama said in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina bar Rabbi Yitzḥak: He departed joyfully, just as it says: “Here he is going out [yotze] to meet you [and he will see you and he will rejoice in his heart]” (Exodus 4:14). Adam the first man encountered him. He said to him: ‘What became of your sentence?’ He said to him: ‘I repented and reached a settlement.’ Adam the first man began beating himself on the face, saying: ‘Such is the power of repentance, and I did not know.’ Immediately, Adam the first man stood and said: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day…” (Psalms 92:1). Rabbi Levi said: Adam the first man said this Psalm, but it was forgotten from his generation, and Moses came and reintroduced it in his own name: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day. It is good to give thanks [lehodot] to the Lord…” (Psalms 92:1–2).”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 18:1: “The root of Amalek within the heart is the absence of awareness of the One before Whom one stands, as it is written in Midrash Tanchuma at the end of Ki Seitzei: The Name is not complete and the Throne is not complete until Amalek is erased. The completeness of the Name is as stated in Pesachim 50a: “I am not read as I am written.” In this world it is not fully evident to the eye how Hashem was, is, and will be, and brings everything into being, which is the meaning of the Name Havayah. The Throne is providence: He sits as a king upon a throne, and His kingship rules over everything. “When Hashem gives you rest”: At first other things, desire, anger, and the like, conceal this. But when a person’s heart is clean and awareness of the One before Whom he stands still does not shine for him—so that he is constantly as one standing before a great king, visibly sensing in everything how Hashem guides and creates, and that there is none besides Him—this comes from the root of Amalek, which must be erased through the service of the heart.”

paragraphs.text:
Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 35:9-10: “But to draw the light and radiance of the Shechinah also upon his body and his animal soul—which is the vital soul actually clothed within his body—he must fulfill practical mitzvos performed through the body itself. Then the actual bodily power involved in this action is included in Hashem’s light and will and united with Him in complete unity; this is the third garment of the divine soul.

Then the power of the vital soul actually within his body, which comes from kelipas nogah, is also transformed from evil to good and actually included in holiness, just like the divine soul itself, since it is precisely this power that acts and performs the mitzvah. Without it, the divine soul would not act within the body at all: it is spiritual, whereas the body is physical and material. The intermediary between them is the vital animal soul clothed in the person’s blood, within his heart and throughout his body.”

אַךְ כְּדֵי לְהַמְשִׁיךְ אוֹר וְהֶאָרַת הַשְּׁכִינָה גַּם עַל גּוּפוֹ וְנַפְשׁוֹ הַבַּהֲמִית, שֶׁהִיא הַחִיּוּנִית הַמְלוּבֶּשֶׁת בְּגוּפוֹ מַמָּשׁ, צָרִיךְ לְקַיֵּים מִצְוֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת הַנַּעֲשׂוֹת עַל יְדֵי הַגּוּף מַמָּשׁ, שֶׁאָז – כֹּחַ הַגּוּף מַמָּשׁ שֶׁבַּעֲשִׂיָּה זוֹ, נִכְלָל בְּאוֹר ה׳ וּרְצוֹנוֹ וּמְיוּחָד בּוֹ בְּיִחוּד גָּמוּר, וְהוּא לְבוּשׁ הַשְּׁלִישִׁי שֶׁל נֶפֶשׁ הָאֱלֹהִית.

וַאֲזַי, גַּם כֹּחַ נֶפֶשׁ הַחִיּוּנִית שֶׁבְּגוּפוֹ מַמָּשׁ שֶׁמִּקְּלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, נִתְהַפֵּךְ מֵרַע לְטוֹב וְנִכְלָל מַמָּשׁ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה כַּנֶּפֶשׁ הָאֱלֹהִית מַמָּשׁ, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא הוּא הַפּוֹעֵל וְעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוָה, שֶׁבִּלְעָדוֹ, לֹא הָיְתָה נֶפֶשׁ הָאֱלֹהִית פּוֹעֶלֶת בַּגּוּף כְּלָל, כִּי הִיא רוּחָנִיִּית, וְהַגּוּף – גַּשְׁמִי וְחוּמְרִי, וְהַמְמוּצָּע בֵּינֵיהֶם, הִיא נֶפֶשׁ הַחִיּוּנִית הַבַּהֲמִית הַמְלוּבֶּשֶׁת בְּדַם הָאָדָם שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ וְכָל הַגּוּף.

p: וְיֵשׁ יִרְאָה עִלָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה, וְכֵן תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁהִיא מִבִּינָה כַּיָּדוּעַ
, Thus there is a supernal fear (yirah ila'ah) and a lower fear (yirah tata'ah), and likewise repentance (teshuvah), which emanates from Binah as is known,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, י
), as it is written: "And his heart will understand (yavin) and he will repent (vashav)" (Isaiah 6:10).
יֵשׁ תְּשׁוּבָה עִלָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה, דְּגַם מִיִּרְאָה בָּא תְּשׁוּבָה
, There is a supernal repentance and a lower repentance, for repentance also comes from fear,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יז.): "תַּכְלִית חָכְמָה תְּשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים", שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה יִרְאַת ה' שֵׂכֶל טוֹב לְכָל עֹשֵׂיהֶם" (תְּהִלִּים קיא, י

) as they stated (Berakhot 17a): "The ultimate goal (takhlit) of wisdom is repentance and good deeds," as it is stated: "The beginning (reishit) of wisdom is the fear of Hashem, good understanding to all who do them" (Psalms 111:10) (
וְהַתַּכְלִית נִקְרָא רֵאשִׁית דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר הָעִיקָּר, וְסוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה
, (for the ultimate goal is called "beginning" reishit, meaning the primary essence, as the final deed is first in initial thought;
וְ"עֹשֵׂיהֶם" הַיְינוּ מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים, וְ"יִרְאַת ה'" הִיא תְּשׁוּבָה
). and "those who do them" refers to good deeds, while "the fear of Hashem" corresponds to repentance).
וְכֵן (בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט.) "אַשְׁרֵי אִישׁ יָרֵא אֶת ה'" – אַשְׁרֵי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה כְּשֶׁהוּא אִישׁ
. And similarly (in Avodah Zarah 19a): "'Praiseworthy is the man who fears Hashem' (Psalms 112:1) – praiseworthy is he who repents while he is still a vigorous man."
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת הֵקִים עוֹלָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, שֶׁמַּכִּיר הַנּוֹכָח

. And King David, peace be upon him, who is the chariot for the attribute of Malchut, established the yoke of repentance (Moed Katan 16b), because he constantly perceived the immediate divine Presence (ha-nokhach).
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת לד:): "הַמֶּלֶךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּרַע שׁוּב אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף
", Therefore they taught (in Berakhot 34b): "Once the king has bowed down in prayer, he does not straighten up again throughout the Amidah,"
וְזֶהוּ מֵרוֹב פַּחַד ה' שֶׁנּוֹפֵל עָלָיו בְּיוֹתֵר מִכָּל אֶחָד
. and this is due to the immense dread of Hashem that falls upon him more than upon anyone else.
וְשָׁם (י רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב): "אֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל הַחֲלוֹמוֹת וְכוּלֵי אַל יִמְנַע מֵהָרַחֲמִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי בְרֹב חֲלוֹמוֹת וַהֲבָלִים וּדְבָרִים הַרְבֵּה כִּי אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים יְרָא" (קֹהֶלֶת ה, ו

). And there (Berakhot 10b top): "Even if the master of dreams tells a person that on the morrow he will die, let him not desist from praying for mercy, as it is stated: 'For in the multitude of dreams and vanities there are many words; rather, fear God'" (Ecclesiastes 5:6).
הִנֵּה בַּכָּתוּב נֶאֱמַר יִרְאָה וְהֵם אָמְרוּ רַחֲמִים דְּהַיְינוּ תְּפִלָּה
, Behold, in the verse "fear" is stated, yet the Sages interpreted it as "mercy," namely prayer;
וְכֵן עַל פָּסוּק "יִירָאוּךָ עִם שָׁמֶשׁ" דָּרְשׁוּ (שָׁם ט:) אַתְּפִלָּה
, and similarly on the verse "They shall fear You with the sun" (Psalms 72:5), they expounded it (Berakhot 9b) as referring to prayer at sunrise,
כִּי עִיקַּר הַתְּפִלָּה בְּהַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכָח לִהְיוֹת עוֹמֵד וּמְדַבֵּר לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ מֶלֶךְ הַמְּלָכִים
. because the essence of prayer lies in recognizing the immediate Presence—standing and speaking directly before the King, King of kings.
וְשַׁבָּת שְׁכִינְתָּא שַׁרְיָא בֵּיהּ, בָּא לְיִרְאָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
, And on Shabbat, when the Shechinah rests within him, one comes to this awe as mentioned above,
וְכֵן מִזֶּה בָּא לִתְשׁוּבָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כב
): and through this one likewise comes to repentance, as they stated (in Bereishit Rabbah, end of Parashah 22): "
כָּךְ כֹּחָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי, מִיָּד אָמַר אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן: מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת וְגוֹמֵר", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. "Such is the power of repentance! Immediately Adam the First proclaimed: 'A Psalm, a Song for the Sabbath day' (Psalms 92:1)," see there.
וְכָל זֶה הָעִיקָּר בְּשַׁבָּת, כִּי דִּירָה לַשְּׁכִינָה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת גּוּף קָדוֹשׁ

p: וְאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה סג) דְּאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נִקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, יְעַיֵּין שָׁם
, And they stated (in Bereishit Rabbah, beginning of Parashah 63) that Abraham and Isaac were also called by the name Israel, see there,
דְּעַל יִצְחָק אָמַר בִּפְשִׁיטוּת, וְעַל אַבְרָהָם שֶׁנִּקְרָא יִשְׂרָאֵל אָמַר שָׁם: "מִילְתָא עֲמִיקְתָּא הִיא", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. where regarding Isaac it states this simply, whereas regarding Abraham being called Israel, Rabbi Nechemiah remarks there: "It is a profound matter (milta amikta hi)," see there.
וְאֵין הַכַּוָּנָה לְעִנְיַן דְּרַשׁ הַפָּסוּק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַמְּפָרְשִׁים שָׁם, דְּמָה עַמְקוּת יֵשׁ בָּזֶה
, Now the intention is not merely regarding the exegetical derivation from the verse, as the commentators wrote there, for what profundity is there in that?
וְהַמִּדְרָשׁ וַדַּאי לֹא יֹאמַר עַל זֶה לְשׁוֹן "מִילְתָא עֲמִיקְתָּא
". The Midrash would certainly not use the expression "it is a profound matter" for a simple textual reading.
וְעַיֵּין זֹהַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית לב עַמּוּד א) עַל פָּסוּק "מְגַלֶּה עֲמֻקּוֹת מִנִּי חֹשֶׁךְ" (אִיּוֹב יב, כב
): Rather, see the Zohar (Bereishit 32a) on the verse "He uncovers deep things (amukot) out of darkness" (Job 12:22): "
אִינּוּן כִּתְרִין עִלָּאִין וְקָרִינַן עֲמֻקּוֹת", עַיֵּין שָׁם
; "These are the supernal crowns, which we call 'deep things' (amukot)," see there;
מַשְׁמַע דַּ"עֲמֻקּוֹת" רָצָה לוֹמַר דָּבָר הַטָּמִיר וְנֶעְלָם וּלְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם
. implying that "deep things" denotes a matter that is concealed, hidden, and beyond human comprehension.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִקְרָא תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים (בַּחֲגִיגָה ג
.), And the explanation is that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, is called the pioneer of proselytes (Chagigah 3a),
כִּי מִתְּחִלָּה עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הָיוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ
, for originally our ancestors were idolaters,
וְהוּא הִכִּיר אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ לְחַד מַאן דְּאָמַר בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה שָׁנָה
; and according to one opinion in the Midrash, he recognized his Creator at forty-eight years of age;
רַק שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הִבְטִיחוֹ: "לְךָ טַל יַלְדֻתֶיךָ" (תְּהִלִּים קיו, ג
), except that the Holy One, blessed be He, promised him: "To you shall the dew of your youth be accounted" (Psalms 110:3),
וְאָמַר (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לט): "מַה טַּל זֶה פּוֹרֵחַ וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם
, and it states (in Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 39): "Just as this dew evaporates and vanishes, so too did his earlier years of idolatry vanish, etc.," see there,
שֶׁפָּרַח וְהָלַךְ לוֹ אוֹתָן שָׁנִים וּכְאִלּוּ אֵינָם
, meaning those prior years evaporated and departed as though they had never been,
וְזָכָה לְשֵׁם "אֵיתָן הָאֶזְרָחִי" דְּהוּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא טו עַמּוּד א
), and he merited the title "Eitan the Ezrachite" (Psalms 89:1), which refers to Abraham our father, as they said (in Bava Batra 15a),
דְּזָכָה לְיִקָּרֵא אֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר מַאן דְּמִשָּׁרְשָׁא וְגִזְעָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזֹּהַר פָּרָשַׁת אֱמוֹר
). for he merited to be called a native-born (ezrach) in Israel, which denotes one who stems from the holy root and stock of Israel, as is written (in Zohar Parashat Emor).
וְזֶהוּ דָּבָר עָמוֹק טָמִיר וְנֶעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה – אֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר לְשַׁנּוֹת הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ
? And this is a profound, hidden, and inscrutable matter in this world: how is it possible to retroactively transform one's very root?
וְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא רַק עַל הַנּוֹלָד בִּקְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
, For the essential name "Israel" applies strictly to one born in the sanctity of Israel (like Isaac),
אֲבָל הַגֵּר נִקְרָא גַּם "בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכַנֶּה" (יְשַׁעְיָה מד, ה) – שֶׁהוּא רַק שֵׁם כִּינּוּי אֶצְלוֹ וְלֹא שֵׁם עֶצֶם

; whereas regarding a convert it is written, "and he shall surname himself (yekhaneh) by the name of Israel" (Isaiah 44:5) – meaning that for him it is only an adopted surname (kinui) rather than an intrinsic name of essence;
אֲבָל מִצַּד הָעֲמוּקּוֹת, שֶׁהוּא מִמַּדְרֵגַת הַכֶּתֶר שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַחָכְמָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל מִלְּשׁוֹן הַזֹּהַר

, yet from the perspective of the "deep things" (amukot), which stems from the level of Keter (the Crown) that transcends Chokhmah (Wisdom), as cited above from the Zohar, his root itself was transformed.

reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: When all the congregations have finished all their prayers, the angel appointed over the prayers takes all the prayers offered in all the congregations, makes them into crowns, and places them upon the head of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is stated: “To You all flesh shall come.” “To You” is interpreted as an ornament, as it is stated: “You shall wear them all as an ornament.” It also says: “Yisrael, in whom I take pride,” for the Holy One, blessed be He, crowns Himself with the prayers of Yisrael, as it is stated: “And a crown of glory upon your head.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: וְכָל כָּךְ לָמָּה, (אלא אינון) אָמְרוּ לֵיהּ, בְּגִין דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא אִתְרָעֵי תָּדִיר בִּצְלוֹתְהוֹן דְּצַדִּיקַיָא וּמִתְעַטֵּר בִּצְלוֹתְהוֹן. כִּדְאַמְרִינָן, דְּהַהוּא מַלְאָכָא דִּמְמַנָּא עַל צְלוֹתְהוֹן דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, סַנְדַּ"לְפוֹן שְׁמֵיהּ, נָטִיל כָּל אִינוּן צְלוֹתִין וְעָבִיד מִנַּיְיהוּ עֲטָרָה לְחֲיֵי הָעוֹלָמִים וְאוּקְמוּהָ. וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן צְלוֹתְהוֹן דְּצַדִּיקַיָּא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא אִתְרָעֵי בְּהוּ וְאִתְעַבְדָן עֲטָרָה לְאִתְעַטְּרָא בְּאִינוּן צְלוֹתִין לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא. וְאִי תֵימָא מַשִּׁרְיָין קַדִּישִׁין הֲווּ אַתְיָין עִמֵּיהּ, אַמַּאי דָּחִיל. אֶלָּא צַדִּיקַיָיא לָא סַמְכִין עַל זְכוּתַיְיהוּ, אֶלָּא עַל צְלוֹתְהוֹן וּבָעוּתְהוֹן לְגַבֵּי מָארֵיהוֹן.
reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: And why is all this? They said to him: Because the Holy One, blessed be He, always desires the prayers of the righteous and crowns Himself with their prayers. As we have said, the angel appointed over the prayers of Yisrael, whose name is Sandalfon, takes all those prayers and makes them into a crown for the Life of the worlds, as they have explained. All the more so the prayers of the righteous, which the Holy One, blessed be He, desires: they become a crown, so that the Holy One, blessed be He, may crown Himself with those prayers. If you ask: Since holy camps were accompanying him, why was he afraid? The righteous rely upon their prayers and petitions to their Master, rather than upon their own merits.

p: וְהוּא קַרְקַפְתָּא דִּתְפִלִּין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמַאֲמַר פָּתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ
, And this level of Keter corresponds to the crown of the head where the tefillin rest (karkafta de-tefillin), as written in the passage Patach Eliyahu,
וּתְפִלִּין שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הוּא הַכֶּתֶר שֶׁעַל הָרֹאשׁ, וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא "פְּאֵר
", for the tefillin of the head is the crown upon the head, and is therefore called "glory" (pe'er),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת יא.) שֶׁזֶּה הַפְּאֵר דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁשֵּׁם ה' נִקְרָא עֲלֵיהֶם
, as they stated (in Berakhot 11a), that this is the glory of Israel—that the Name of Hashem is called upon them,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם ו.) דְּהֵם עֹז לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, דִּכְתִיב: "וְרָאוּ כָּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ כִּי שֵׁם ה' נִקְרָא עָלֶיךָ" (דְּבָרִים כח, י) – אֵלּוּ תְּפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ

. and as they stated (Berakhot 6a) that they are strength to Israel, as it is written: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of Hashem is called upon you" (Deuteronomy 28:10) – these are the tefillin of the head.
וּתְפִלִּין דְּמָרֵי עָלְמָא אָמַר שָׁם דְּהֵם נִקְרָאִים עֻזּוֹ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְדִכְתִיב בְּהוּ: "מִי כְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ", עַיֵּין שָׁם

. And regarding the tefillin of the Master of the Universe, it states there that they are called the strength of Hashem, blessed be He, and that in them is inscribed: "Who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the earth" (I Chronicles 17:21), see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל פְּאֵר דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר בְּךָ אֶתְפָּאָר" (יְשַׁעְיָה מט, ג
), This means that Israel is the glory of Hashem, blessed be He, as it is written: "Israel, in whom I will be glorified" (Isaiah 49:3),
וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים וְגוֹמֵר מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַי לְהִתְפָּאֵר" (שָׁם ס, כא
). and it is stated: "And Your people are all righteous... the work of My hands, in whom I may be glorified" (Isaiah 60:21).
וְכֵן אִיתָא (בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב
): And similarly it is found (in Vayikra Rabbah, Parashah 2):
מָשָׁל לְאֶחָד שֶׁעָשָׂה עֲטָרָה לַמֶּלֶךְ וְכוּלֵי, כָּל מַה שֶּׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּעַ בָּהּ אֲבָנִים טוֹבוֹת וּמַרְגָּלִיּוֹת קְבַע, שֶׁעָתִיד לִינָּתֵן בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ
; "A parable of one who was fashioning a crown for a king... 'Whatever precious stones and pearls you are able to set within it, set them, for it is destined to be placed upon the head of the king';
כָּךְ אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה: כָּל מַה שֶּׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לְשַׁבֵּחַ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שַׁבַּח, לָמָּה? שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לְהִתְפָּאֵר בָּהֶן וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. so too the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: 'Whatever praise you are able to lavish upon Israel, praise them; why? Because I am destined to be glorified through them, etc.,'" see there.
הֲרֵי דְּהִמְשִׁילָם לַעֲטָרָה בְּרֹאשׁ הַמֶּלֶךְ מֶלֶךְ הַמְּלָכִים
. Behold, He compared them to a crown upon the head of the King, the King of kings. (

), (And in Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 21) it states that out of the prayers of Israel crowns are woven upon the head of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is stated: "O You Who hear prayer, unto You—as Your ornament (adekha)—all flesh shall come" (Psalms 65:3),
וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: "יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר בְּךָ אֶתְפָּאָר" וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַעֲטֶרֶת תִּפְאֶרֶת בְּיַד אֱלֹהָיִךְ" (יְשַׁעְיָה סב, ג), עַיֵּין שָׁם
, and thus it states: "Israel, in whom I will be glorified," etc., as it is stated: "And a crown of glory in the hand of your God" (Isaiah 62:3), see there;
וְנִזְכָּר בַּתּוֹסָפוֹת (חֲגִיגָה יג:) דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וְקוֹשֵׁר, וּבַזֹּהַר (וַיִּשְׁלַח קסז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב, בְּשַׁלַּח נח עַמּוּד א), עַיֵּין שָׁם
. and this is mentioned in Tosafot (Chagigah 13b, s.v. Ve-kosher) and in the Zohar (Vayishlach 167b end; Beshalach 58a), see there.

p: וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמַאֲמַר פָּתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ: "כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן אִיהוּ כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת, וַעֲלֵיהּ אִתְּמַר: מַגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית" (יְשַׁעְיָה מו, י

). And this aligns with what is written in Patach Eliyahu: "The Supernal Crown (Keter Elyon) is the Crown of Sovereignty (Keter Malchut), and concerning it Scripture states: 'Declaring the end (acharit) from the beginning (reishit)'" (Isaiah 46:10).
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַכֶּתֶר בְּרֹאשׁ מֶלֶךְ עַל הוֹרָאַת מַלְכוּתוֹ
, This means that the crown upon a king's head signifies his sovereignty (Malchut),
וְהוּא כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִים עֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ
, which is realized only when there are subjects who willingly accept the yoke of his sovereignty;
וְעַל זֶה הָיָה בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם לְגַלּוֹת כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ
. and for this very purpose the world was created—to reveal the glory of His kingship.
וְזֶהוּ: "בְּרֵאשִׁית" – בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ רֵאשִׁית, שֶׁהֵם הַמַּכִּירִים כְּבוֹדוֹ וּמְקַבְּלִים אֲדוֹנוּתוֹ וּמַלְכוּתוֹ

. And this is the exposition of Rashi: "'In the beginning (Bereishit)' – for the sake of Israel who are called 'beginning' (reishit)," for they are the ones who recognize His glory and accept His mastery and kingship.
וּבִתְפִלָּה, שֶׁהוּא אָז עוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
, And in prayer, when one stands directly before the King as mentioned above,
וּ"כְעֵינֵי עֲבָדִים אֶל יַד אֲדוֹנֵיהֶם כֵּן עֵינֵינוּ אֶל ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ" (תְּהִלִּים קכג, ב) – מִזֶּה הוּא הַכֶּתֶר
. as in "Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master... so our eyes look to Hashem our God" (Psalms 123:2)—out of this submissive recognition the supernal Crown is formed.
וְזֶהוּ עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת דְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת
: And this corresponds to the ten utterances of Creation, which parallel the ten sefirot:
וְהַתְחָלַת הִתְגַּלּוּת מַאֲמָר הוּא "וַיְהִי אוֹר", שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַחָכְמָה
, the beginning of manifest utterance is "Let there be light" (Genesis 1:3), which represents the revelation of Chokhmah (Wisdom),
דְּבָזֶה יֵשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת לָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "שֶׁחָלַק מֵחָכְמָתוֹ לִירֵאָיו" (בְּרָכוֹת נח
.). for in Chokhmah there is comprehension accessible to man, as we bless: "Who has imparted of His wisdom to those who fear Him" (Berakhot 58a).
וּ"בְרֵאשִׁית" נַמִּי מַאֲמָר (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לב.), אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "וַיֹּאמֶר
", "In the beginning (Bereishit)" is also counted as one of the ten utterances (Rosh Hashanah 32a), except that the word "And He said (vayomer)" is not stated in it,
כִּי הוּא הַשֵּׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן, "יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים יח, יב), וְהוּא טָמִיר וְנֶעְלָם מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם

. because it corresponds to Keter, the Primordial Intellect concealed from all thought, concerning which it is written "He makes darkness His secret place" (Psalms 18:12), remaining hidden and inscrutable beyond human grasp.
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל עָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה, וְהַיְינוּ בְּהָרֵאשִׁית שֶׁל מַחֲשָׁבָה
, Now Israel arose first in divine thought, namely within the "beginning" (Reishit / Keter) of Supernal Thought,
וְזֶה "מַגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית
", and this is the secret of "declaring the end (acharit / Malchut) from the beginning (reishit / Keter)":
כִּי הָאָדָם נִבְרָא אָחוֹר לְמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית, כִּי הַתַּכְלִית הוּא בַּסּוֹף וְהוּא רֵאשִׁית הַמְּכֻוָּון בַּבְּרִיאָה
. for man was created last at the conclusion of the six days of Creation, because the ultimate purpose manifests at the end while standing first in the original intention of Creation.

; Prior to the sin of Adam, in accordance with "God made man upright" (Ecclesiastes 7:29), all of his seed would have been holy, as mentioned above;
וּמִשֶּׁקִּלְקֵל הָיָה שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תֹּהוּ, עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָב אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית
, but once he corrupted his way, there ensued two thousand years of spiritual desolation (Tohu), until Abraham arrived as the father of the Israelite nation,
וְהוּא עִיקַּר מְכֻוָּון הַבְּרִיאָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יב): "'בְּהִבָּרְאָם' – בְּאַבְרָהָם

", and he fulfilled the primary intention of Creation, as they expounded (in Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 12): "'When they were created (be-hibar'am)' (Genesis 2:4) – with the letters of Be-Avraham (through Abraham),"
וְשָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ: "'בְּהִבָּרְאָם' – בְּהֵ"א בְּרָאָם", וְכֵן אִיתָא (בִּמְנָחוֹת כט:) דְּבְהֵ"א נִבְרָא עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, עַיֵּין שָׁם
. and immediately following there: "'Be-hibar'am' – with the letter Hei He created them," and similarly it is stated (in Menachot 29b) that this world was created with the letter Hei, see there.
וְהוּא הֵ"א אַחֲרוֹנָה דְּשֵׁם, מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת, שְׁכִינַת עֻזּוֹ הַשּׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
. And this is the final Hei of the Tetragrammaton, the attribute of Malchut, the Shechinah of His strength Who dwells amidst the children of Israel.
וּבְאַבְרָהָם נִתּוֹסֵף הַהֵ"א כְּשֶׁנִּצְטַוָּה עַל הַמִּילָה
, And in Abraham this letter Hei was added to his name when he was commanded regarding circumcision,
שֶׁאָז נַעֲשָׂה בְּשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ וְנִתְקַדֵּשׁ גּוּפוֹ בִּקְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְנַעֲשָׂה לִבּוֹ מָדוֹר לַשְּׁכִינָה
. for then he became "holy flesh," his body was sanctified with the holiness of Israel, and his heart became a permanent abode for the Shechinah.
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (לֶךְ לְךָ צד עַמּוּד א) פָּתַח הַשְּׁלִישִׁי עַל פָּסוּק "וּמִבְּשָׂרִי אֶחֱזֶה
", And in the holy Zohar (Lech Lecha 94a), the third sage opened his discourse on the verse "And from my flesh I shall behold God,"
דִּכְשֶׁנִּימּוֹל מִינֵיהּ חָמֵי לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא מִנֵּיהּ מַמָּשׁ, וְנִשְׁמְתָא קַדִּישָׁא אִתְאֲחִידַת בֵּיהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם
, teaching that when one is circumcised, from within himself he beholds the Holy One, blessed be He, literally from his own flesh, and the holy soul becomes bound within him, see there;
וּמֵבִיא פָּסוּק: "מִנִּשְׁמַת אֵלּוֹהַּ יֹאבֵדוּ" (אִיּוֹב ד, ט
) – and it cites the verse "From the breath (nishmat) of God..." (Job 4:9) –
מְבוֹאָר דִּנְשָׁמָה קַדִּישָׁא דְּקָאָמַר הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהוּא חֵלֶק ה' וּצְרוֹרָא דִּלְעֵילָא שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
, making it clear that the "holy soul" of which it speaks is that which is a literal portion of Hashem and the supernal bundle of life, namely Knesset Yisrael,

. which is embodied in the letter Hei that was added to him at that time.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה אֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְפָּאֵר בּוֹ

וּתְחִלַּת מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַבְּרִיאָה בִּשְׁבִילוֹ
; and the primordial thought of Creation was for his sake;
דְּ"עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" שֶׁהֵם נִימּוֹלִים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, מְסַיֵּים אוֹתוֹ כָּתוּב: "מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַי לְהִתְפָּאֵר
", for on the verse "And Your people are all righteous"—referring to their being circumcised as mentioned above—that very verse concludes: "the work of My hands, in whom I may be glorified,"

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 25b:11: “Rav Yehuda said: Opposite a naked gentile, it is forbidden to recite Shema. The Gemara asks: Why did Rav Yehuda discuss particularly the case of a gentile? Even with regard to a Jew it is also prohibited. The Gemara replies: Opposite the nakedness of a Jew, it is obvious that it is prohibited; however, opposite the nakedness of a gentile, it was necessary for him to say. Lest you say that since it is written about gentiles: “Their flesh is the flesh of donkeys” (Ezekiel 23:20), say that his nakedness is like that of a mere donkey and does not constitute nakedness. Rav Yehuda taught us that their nakedness is also considered nakedness, as it is written regarding the sons of Noah: “And their father’s nakedness they did not see” (Genesis 9:23). Although Noah predated Abraham and was consequently not Jewish, his nakedness is mentioned.”

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Megillah 20b:4:2: ““The night was for us a watch.” This is difficult: In Berachos 2b, concerning the emergence of the stars, we say that it is night; although there is no proof, there is an indication, as it is written, “The night was for us a watch.” Why is it not a complete proof, as the verse is used here? The answer is that there the aim is to establish that the time for lying down, concerning the recitation of Shema, is the emergence of the stars. Therefore it says there that this is not a complete proof: Although it is night at that time, it is nevertheless not the time when everyone lies down.”

דְּעִיקַּר שֵׁם בָּשָׂר עַל אֵבֶר הָעֶרְוָה וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, וְכֵן בִּבְרָכוֹת הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל מַיְיתֵי לַהּ אַעֶרְוַת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
, even though the primary term "flesh" (basar) refers to the reproductive organ as noted above—and indeed in Berakhot (25b) they cite this verse regarding the nakedness of idolaters,
כִּדְמְסַיֵּים: "וְזִרְמַת סוּסִים זִרְמָתָם
", as the verse concludes: "and whose issue is the issue of horses"— (
וּבִבְרָכוֹת נח.) דְּאָמַר דְּבָא עַל חֲמָרְתָּא וְכוּלֵי דִּכְתִיב: "אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׂר וְגוֹמֵר
", (and in Berakhot 58a) where Rav Shila said that one who cohabits with a she-donkey, etc., because it is written: "Whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys,"
גַּם כָּל הַגּוּף נִקְרָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה כֵּן, כִּי אֵינָם מִכְּלַל אָדָם
nevertheless, their entire physical body is likewise designated thus on account of this, because they are not included in the spiritual category of "Adam" (man) (
וּבְנִדָּה מה. מַיְיתֵי מִזֶּה גַּם לְעִנְיַן דְּטִבְעָתָם מְשׁוּנָּה מִטֶּבַע בְּנֵי אָדָם
, (and in Niddah 45a the Gemara cites this verse even regarding the fact that their physical constitution differs from the nature of Israel,
וּמִשָּׁם רְאִיָּה דְּלֹא עַל הָאֵבֶר דַּוְוקָא קָאָמַר דְּהוּא נִקְרָא בָּשָׂר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, רַק עַל כָּל הַגּוּף, עַיֵּין שָׁם
). which proves that the verse does not speak exclusively of the reproductive organ being called flesh, but rather of the entire body, see there).
וְהָא דְּנָקַט חֲמוֹר טְפֵי מִכָּל בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים, הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּעֵרָכִין יט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב
) Now as to why Scripture singled out a donkey more than any other animal, one might have suggested it is based on what is taught (in Arachin 19b top
בְּאוֹמֵר "מִשְׁקַל יָדִי וְרַגְלִי עָלַי", שׁוֹקֵל בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ
, regarding one who vows, "The weight of my hand or my foot is incumbent upon me," that he estimates the weight using donkey flesh,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאִיָּה לַדָּבָר זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר: "אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים וְגוֹמֵר
"; "and even though there is no conclusive proof for the matter, there is an allusion to the matter: 'Whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys'" (since donkey flesh has the same density as human flesh);
וְאִם כֵּן יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּמִשּׁוּם דְּשָׁוֶה מִשְׁקַל בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹר לִבְשַׂר אָדָם קָרֵי לְהוּ כֵּן
. and if so, one could say that because the specific gravity of donkey flesh equals that of human flesh, Scripture calls them thus.
אֲבָל אִי רַק מִטַּעַם זֶה נִקְרָא בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים, אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ רְאִיָּה גְּמוּרָה מֵהָתָם, וּמַאי "אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאִיָּה לַדָּבָר" דְּקָאָמַר

? However, if it were called "flesh of donkeys" solely for this physical reason, then that verse would constitute a complete proof, so why did the Tanna state "even though there is no proof for the matter"?
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ פָּרִיךְ הַגְּמָרָא (בְּנִדָּה ח סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): "זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר? הֲרֵי רְאִיָּה גְּדוֹלָה הִיא
!", Indeed, the Gemara raises an identical challenge (in Niddah 8b end): "Merely an allusion to the matter? Behold, it is a great proof!"
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה הִקְשׁוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (בִּמְגִילָּה כ:) דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וְהָיוּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם
. and Tosafot posed a similar question (in Megillah 20b, s.v. Ve-hayu), see there.
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּיֵשׁ עוֹד טַעַם אַחֵר בָּזֶה
. Perforce, there is another, deeper reason for this.

p: וַעֲבָדִים דְּאָמַר (בִּיבָמוֹת סב סוֹף עַמּוּד א) דְּאֵין לָהֶם יַחַס לְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל, דִּכְתִיב: "שְׁבוּ לָכֶם פֹּה עִם הַחֲמוֹר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כב, ה) – עַם הַדּוֹמֶה לַחֲמוֹר

, Now regarding Canaanite slaves, concerning whom it is stated (in Yevamot 62a end) that according to all opinions they lack halakhic lineage, as it is written: "Abide you here with (im) the donkey" (Genesis 22:5) – expounded as "a people (am) similar to a donkey,"
וְאַף שֶׁהֵם נִימּוֹלִים, דְּמָלוּ וְטָבְלוּ לְשֵׁם עַבְדוּת וְחַיָּיבִים בְּמִצְווֹת כְּנָשִׁים
, even though they are circumcised—having been circumcised and immersed for the sake of servitude, becoming obligated in mitzvot like women—
וְכֵן אִיתָא (בָּבָא קַמָּא מט.) בְּנוֹגֵחַ שִׁפְחָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת דַּחֲמָרְתָּא מְעַבַּרְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא דְּאַזִּיק, מֵהַאי קְרָא
, and similarly it is stated (in Bava Kamma 49a) regarding an ox that gores a pregnant maidservant, that it is treated merely as having damaged a pregnant she-donkey, derived from this same verse,
אַף דְּחַיָּיבוֹת בְּמִצְווֹת כְּנָשִׁים יִשְׂרְאֵלִיּוֹת
, even though maidservants are obligated in mitzvot like Israelite women, (
וּבַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יג:) אִיתָא עַל עֶבֶד שֶׁמַּכְנִיסוֹ תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם
, (and in Avodah Zarah 13b) it is stated regarding purchasing a slave that one brings him under the wings of the Shechinah, see there, (
וּבְקִדּוּשִׁין סב רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) אִיתָא: "מֵעִיקָּרָא בְּהֵמָה וְכוּלֵי
", (yet in Kiddushin 62b top) it states regarding a maidservant: "Initially she was categorized as an animal, etc.,"
וְכֵן (שָׁם סט.) בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק ג: "וְלַד מְעֵי שִׁפְחָה כִּוְלַד בִּמְעֵי בְּהֵמָה
", and likewise (Kiddushin 69a) at the end of the third chapter: "The fetus in the womb of a maidservant is like the fetus in the womb of an animal,"
וְהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן מֵהַאי קְרָא דַּחֲמוֹר מִין בְּהֵמָה
which also derives from this verse, since a donkey is a species of animal (
וּבְנִדָּה יז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א: "וְאִינְהוּ מַאי דְּרוּשׁ וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם דְּרָצוּ לְדַמּוֹתָם לִבְהֵמָה לְגַמְרֵי
), (and in Niddah 17a top: "And how did they expound it, etc.," see there that they sought to compare them entirely to an animal),
וּבַגְּמָרָא דִּיבָמוֹת שָׁם מְבוֹאָר דַּעֲבָדִים גְּרִיעֵי בָּזֶה מֵעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, דְּהֵם אֵינָם כַּחֲמוֹר
, and in the Gemara in Yevamot there it is clear that slaves are inferior in this respect to free gentiles, who are not legally categorized as donkeys regarding lineage,
וְכֵן הוּא (בְּקִדּוּשִׁין סח סוֹף עַמּוּד א) דְּשִׁפְחָה לֹא תָּפְסֵי קִדּוּשִׁין מֵהַאי טַעְמָא דְּדוֹמֶה לַחֲמוֹר
, and so it is (in Kiddushin 68a end) that betrothal (kiddushin) does not take effect with a maidservant for this reason that she is compared to a donkey,
וְשָׁם רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב: "נָכְרִית מְנָלַן?" – הֲרֵי דְּלֹא אָמְרוּ זֶה אֶלָּא בַּעֲבָדִים

. while at the top of 68b the Gemara asks: "From where do we know that betrothal does not take effect with a gentile woman?" – proving that "a people similar to a donkey" was said strictly regarding slaves.

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּבֵית מוֹתְבָא רַבָּא, מָה נִשְׁתַּנּוּ פִּטְרֵי חֲמוֹרִים מִפִּטְרֵי סוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים? אָמַר לִי: גְּזֵירַת הַכָּתוּב הִיא, וְעוֹד שֶׁסִּיְּיעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁעַת יְצִיאָתָם מִמִּצְרַיִם, שֶׁאֵין לָךְ כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ עִמּוֹ תִּשְׁעִים חֲמוֹרִים לוּבִים טְעוּנִים מִכַּסְפָּהּ וּזְהָבָהּ שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם.

p: וְהַיְינוּ דְּעֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי שֶׁגּוּפוֹ קָנוּי לַאֲדוֹנוֹ לְעָבְדוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא כַּחֲמוֹר שֶׁקָּנוּי לִבְעָלָיו לַעֲבוֹד וּלְמַשָּׂא

, The explanation is that a Canaanite slave, whose physical body is legally acquired as the property of his master to serve him, is like a donkey, which is acquired by its owner for labor and carrying burdens,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה:): "יָשִׂים עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּשׁוֹר לְעֹל וְכַחֲמוֹר לְמַשָּׂאוֹי
". as expressed in the phrasing of the Gemara (Avodah Zarah 5b): "One should place himself upon words of Torah like an ox to the yoke and like a donkey to the burden."
וְשׁוֹר, אַף דְּגַם כֵּן לְמַשָּׂא, עִלּוּיָא דִּידֵיהּ הוּא עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילַת בְּשָׂרוֹ וּלְכָךְ נוֹצַר
; Now an ox, even though it is also used for draft labor, reaches its ultimate elevation through the consumption of its flesh, and for that purpose it was created;
אֲבָל הַחֲמוֹר נוֹצַר רַק לְעַבְדוּת הָאָדָם וְהוּא מְיוּחָד לְכָךְ
. whereas the donkey was created exclusively for the service of man, and is uniquely designated for that role.
וּבִלְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים פֶּרֶק עַרְבֵי פְסָחִים קיח.): "זָלְגוּ עֵינָיו דְּמָעוֹת, אָמַר: אֲנִי וַחֲמוֹרוֹ נֹאכַל בְּאֵבוּס אֶחָד

?!" – And in the wording of the Gemara (Pesachim, chapter Arvei Pesachim 118a): "Adam's eyes flowed with tears when told 'you shall eat the herb of the field'; he said: Shall I and my donkey eat from the same manger?!" –
נָקַט חֲמוֹר מִכָּל בַּעַל חַיִּים, שֶׁהוּא הַמְּיוּחָד לְעַבְדוּת הָאָדָם
. he singled out the donkey from among all animals because it is the creature specifically designated for man's service.
וְהָעֶבֶד, אַף שֶׁאֵין קָרוּי "בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים", שֶׁהוּא נִימּוֹל וְיֵשׁ חוֹתַם הַבְּרִית בִּבְשָׂרוֹ
, Thus the Canaanite slave—even though his flesh is not called "the flesh of donkeys," since he is circumcised and bears the seal of the covenant in his flesh,
וְאֵינוֹ בִּכְלַל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וּבַר מִצְווֹת וְתַחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
and he has left the category of idolaters, is obligated in mitzvot, and stands under the wings of the Shechinah, as noted above (
וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין נח:) דְּעֶבֶד יָצָא מִכְּלַל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְלִכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא בָּא
, (and in Sanhedrin 58b) that a slave has departed from the category of gentiles yet has not entered the full category of Israel, (
וּבְהוֹרָיוֹת יג סוֹף עַמּוּד א) דְּגָדֵל עִמָּנוּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
; (and in Horayot 13a end) that he grows with us in holiness—
אֲבָל גַּם בַּחֲמוֹרִים דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ מַעֲלָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּחֲמוֹרוֹ דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר וּדְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא (בְּשַׁבָּת קיב סוֹף עַמּוּד ב
), nevertheless, just as even among the donkeys of Israel there is a unique spiritual elevation, as told of the donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair and that of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa (Shabbat 112b end),
וְכֵן נִתְקַדְּשׁוּ פִּטְרֵי חֲמוֹרִים, וְאָמְרוּ (בְּכוֹרוֹת ה רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) לְפִי שֶׁסִּיְּיעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּבִיזַּת מִצְרַיִם
, and similarly the firstborn of donkeys were sanctified in the Torah, which our Sages explained (Bekhorot 5b top) was because they assisted Israel in carrying the spoils of Egypt,
וְהַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁהֵם עֲבָדִים דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל – וְעַל כֵּן הָעֶבֶד נִמְשַׁל גַּם כֵּן לַחֲמוֹר
. precisely because they serve as the property and servants of Israel—so too the slave, being legally acquired for servitude, is compared to a donkey.

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם — דְּבָרָיו נִשְׁמָעִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״סוֹף דָּבָר הַכֹּל נִשְׁמָע אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים יְרָא וְגוֹ׳״. מַאי ״כִּי זֶה כׇּל הָאָדָם״? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה. רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: שָׁקוּל זֶה כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא לִצְווֹת לָזֶה.

Rabbi Elazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said: The entire world was created only for this person. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: This person is equal in weight to the entire world. Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai says—and some say Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma says: The entire world was created only to provide companionship for this person.

p: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִצְרִי עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָנוּי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
, In contrast, an Egyptian idolater who is not legally acquired as property by Israel
וְהֵם נִקְרָא בְּשָׂרָם "בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹר" שֶׁאֵין קְרוּיִם אָדָם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
, has his flesh called "the flesh of donkeys" because they are not termed "Adam" and lack the covenant of circumcision, as explained above,
אֲבָל אֵינָם בִּכְלַל "עַם הַדּוֹמֶה לַחֲמוֹר" כֵּיוָן דְּאֵין קְנוּיִם לְעַבְדוּת
; yet they are not in the legal category of "a people similar to a donkey" regarding lineage, since their bodies are not acquired in servitude;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הִמְשִׁילָם לַחֲמוֹר לְפִי שֶׁעִיקַּר יְצִירָתָם הָיָה גַּם כֵּן רַק לְצוֹרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְעַבְדוּתָם
, nonetheless, the prophet compared their flesh to that of a donkey because the ultimate purpose of their creation was likewise solely for the sake of Israel and their service,
וּכְמוֹ לֶעָתִיד: "וְעָמְדוּ זָרִים וְרָעוּ צֹאנְכֶם וּבְנֵי נֵכָר אִכָּרֵיכֶם וְכֹרְמֵיכֶם, וְאַתֶּם כֹּהֲנֵי ה' תִּקָּרֵאוּ מְשָׁרְתֵי אֱלֹהֵינוּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה סא, ה-ו

). as will be manifest in the future: "And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the foreigner shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers; but you shall be called the priests of Hashem, the ministers of our God" (Isaiah 61:5-6).
וּבִשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה נִבְחֲרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכָךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ לִי מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים וְגוֹי קָדוֹשׁ" (שְׁמוֹת יט, ו
), Indeed, at the time of the Giving of the Torah, Israel was chosen for this very station, as it is written: "And you shall be unto Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation" (Exodus 19:6),
וְהַכֹּהֲנִים פְּנוּיִם רַק לַעֲבוֹדַת ה', דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא נָטְלוּ חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ וַה' חֶלְקָם
, and the priests are free exclusively for the service of Hashem—which is why they took no territorial portion in the Land, Hashem being their portion—
וְהֵם נוֹטְלִים מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְפַרְנָסָתָם
; and they receive the priestly gifts from the children of Israel for their sustenance;
וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִבְחֲרוּ לִהְיוֹת כֹּהֲנֵי ה', וְהָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת יַעֲשׂוּ צָרְכֵי גּוּפָם
. so too all of Israel were chosen to be the priests of Hashem, while the nations of the world attend to their material needs.
וְאָמְרוּ (בְּעֵירוּבִין מג:) דְּכֵיוָן דְּאָתֵי מְשִׁיחָא לֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ לִטְרוֹחַ עוֹד גַּם בְּצוֹרֶךְ שַׁבָּת וְיוֹם טוֹב, עַיֵּין שָׁם
, And they stated (in Eruvin 43b) that once the Messiah comes, Israel will no longer need to toil even in the preparations for Shabbat and Yom Tov, see there, (
וּבְשַׁבָּת לב:) דְּהַזָּהִיר בְּצִיצִית מְשַׁמְּשִׁין לוֹ שְׁמוֹנֶה וְעֶשְׂרִים מֵאוֹת עֲבָדִים
, (and in Shabbat 32b) that whoever is meticulous in the mitzvah of tzitzit will be waited upon by two thousand eight hundred servants;
וְאַף שֶׁיִּשָּׁאֲרוּ אָז רַק הַכְּשֵׁרִין, יִהְיֶה רִיבּוּי בָּהֶם כָּל כָּךְ שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יִצְטָרֵךְ אָז לְכָל כָּךְ עֲבָדִים
. and even though only the upright among the nations will remain then, there will be such an abundance of them that each individual in Israel will have that many servants.
וְאִם כֵּן, אַף דְּאֵינָם עַתָּה עֲבָדִים בְּפֹעַל לִהְיוֹת דּוֹמִין בְּפֹעַל לַחֲמוֹר
, Consequently, even though they are not currently servants in actuality so as to be legally equated to a donkey,
בְּשָׂרָם שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּשַׂר אָדָם אָמַר שֶׁהוּא בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹר, כִּי עִיקַּר יְצִירָתָם הוּא לְכָךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
, Scripture terms their flesh—which is not sanctified as the flesh of "Adam"—"the flesh of donkeys," because the underlying purpose of their creation in this world is for that service,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת ו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): "כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה וּלְצַוּוֹת לָזֶה
". just as our Sages taught (in Berakhot 6b end): "The entire world was created solely for the sake of this one (who fears Heaven) and to serve as company for this one".

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 145:1: “In every human action, the deed is like a body and the thought is its soul; a body without a soul is nothing. p: (וּבַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ב:) שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁעָשׂוּ לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיַּעַסְקוּ בַּתּוֹרָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם

. (And in Avodah Zarah 2b) it relates that in the future the nations will claim before God that everything they built—markets, bathhouses, and bridges—they did solely for the sake of Israel, so that Israel might engage in Torah study, see there.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה תָּמוּהַּ, אֵיךְ יִהְיוּ שׁוֹטִים כָּאֵלּוּ לוֹמַר שֶׁקֶר מְפוּרְסָם כָּזֶה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
? Now this is seemingly astonishing: how could they be such fools as to utter such a blatant falsehood before the Holy One, blessed be He?
וְהֵם נִכְנָסִין לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיטּוֹל שְׂכַר עֲבוֹדָתָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְיַאֲמִינוּ אָז בְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
, For they are entering before the Holy One, blessed be He, to receive reward for their labor in this world, fully believing then in the Holy One, blessed be He;
וְאֵיךְ יַעֲלֶה עַל לִבָּם לְהַטְעוֹתוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי שֶׁקֶר הַיָּדוּעַ לַכֹּל, שֶׁעָשׂוּ הַכֹּל לְצוֹרֶךְ עַצְמָם, וְהָיוּ עוֹד שׂוֹנְאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמְשַׁעְבְּדִים בָּהֶם

? how then could it enter their minds to deceive Him with a lie known to all, when they manifestly built everything for their own selfish needs, and were furthermore haters of Israel who subjugated them?
וְהַגַּם דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵשִׁיב לָהֶם כֵּן: "שׁוֹטִים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם, כָּל מַה שֶּׁעֲשִׂיתֶם לְצוֹרֶךְ עַצְמְכֶם עֲשִׂיתֶם וְכוּלֵי", מִכָּל מָקוֹם מָה רָאוּ הֵם לוֹמַר כֵּן

? And even though the Holy One, blessed be He, indeed replies to them thus: "Fools of the world! Everything you did, you did for your own sake, etc.," nevertheless, what possessed them to make such a claim in the first place?
וְגַם לָמָּה קְרָאָם "שׁוֹטִים" וְלֹא "שַׁקְרָנִים
"? Furthermore, why did He call them "fools" (shotim) rather than "liars" (shakranim)?
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת כָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אַף שֶׁהֵם עוֹשִׂים לְצוֹרֶךְ עַצְמָם
, However, in truth, regarding all their undertakings in this world—even though they act purely for their own self-interest—

כְּבָר בֵּיאֵר זֶה הָרַמְבַּ"ם בְּהַקְדָּמַת פֵּירוּשׁ הַמִּשְׁנָה, שֶׁיִּבְנֶה אָדָם אַרְמוֹן וְיִטַּע כֶּרֶם יָקָר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְתוֹעֶלֶת חָסִיד אֶחָד בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים, שֶׁיֶּחֱסֶה בְּאֶחָד מֵהַקִּירוֹת יוֹם אֶחָד וְיִשְׁתֶּה כּוֹס יַיִן אֶחָד מֵהַכֶּרֶם

the Rambam has already explained in his Introduction to the Commentary on the Mishnah that a person may build a grand palace and plant a costly vineyard which in the end of days serves solely to benefit a single pious man who takes shelter beside one of its walls for a day or drinks a single cup of wine from that vineyard to sustain himself (
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מ עַמּוּד ב בְּכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה: "בָּרוּךְ שֶׁמָּסַר עוֹלָמוֹ לְשׁוֹמְרִים", עַיֵּין שָׁם), יְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּעִיּוּן
. (and along the lines of what they stated in Avodah Zarah 40b in a similar vein: "Blessed is He Who entrusted His world to guardians," see there), examine the Rambam there well.
וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִזֶּה תּוֹעֶלֶת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה
. Thus, all of their worldly enterprises exist only because Hashem, blessed be He, willed that benefit should ultimately accrue from them for Israel to engage in Torah.
וּכְשֶׁיַּכִּירוּ שֶׁהַכֹּל הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת לְצוֹרֶךְ כָּךְ
, And in the World to Come, when the nations retrospectively perceive that in objective reality all their labor was orchestrated by Providence for Israel's Torah study,
יַחְשְׁבוּ הֵם שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם לֹא כִּוְּונוּ לָזֶה, סוֹף סוֹף מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם רְצוּיִים וְיִרְצוּ לְקַבֵּל שָׂכָר עַל זֶה
. they will imagine that even though they had no such intention at the time, since their deeds ultimately fulfilled this purpose, they are entitled to claim reward for it.
וְעַל זֶה יֹאמַר לָהֶם: "שׁוֹטִים וְכוּלֵי", שֶׁקְּרָאָם רַק שׁוֹטִים
, And to this He will reply to them: "Fools of the world!", calling them "fools" rather than liars,
שֶׁזֶּה שְׁטוּת לְבַקֵּשׁ שָׂכָר עַל מַה שֶּׁהֵם לֹא כִּיוְּונוּ לָזֶה, וְ"רַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי" וַ"ה' יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב" (שְׁמוּאֵל א טז, ז
), because it is sheer folly to demand reward for an outcome they never intended, for "the Merciful One desires the heart" and "Hashem looks to the heart" (I Samuel 16:7);
וּמַה שֶּׁנִּסְתּוֹבֵב לְצוֹרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל זֶהוּ מַעֲשֵׂה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְהֵם לֹא פָּעֲלוּ זֶה
. and the fact that their actions resulted in benefit for Israel was entirely the work of Hashem, blessed be He, not their doing.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם שַׁפִּיר קָרוּ לְהוּ מִטַּעַם זֶה "בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים
", Nevertheless, for this very reason Scripture rightly calls them "the flesh of donkeys,"
כֵּיוָן דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקַּר יְצִירַת גּוּפָם וְכָל פְּעוּלָתָם הַכֹּל לְשִׁימּוּשׁ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
. since the fundamental purpose of their physical creation and all their activity is entirely to serve Israel.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 58a:4: “He used to say: How many labors the first man performed before finding bread to eat! He plowed, sowed, reaped, gathered sheaves, threshed, winnowed, sorted, ground, sifted, kneaded, and baked, and only then ate. Yet I rise early and find all of these prepared before me. How many labors the first man performed before finding a garment to wear! He sheared, washed, combed, spun, and wove, and only then found a garment to wear. Yet I rise early and find all of these prepared before me. All the nations labor and come to the entrance of my house, and I rise early and find all of these before me.”
