אַל תִּקְרֵי חָרוּת אֶלָּא חֵירוּת, שֶׁאֵין לְךָ בֶּן חוֹרִין אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁעוֹסֵק בְּתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה
", "Do not read charut (engraved upon the tablets) but cheirut (freedom), for you have no truly free person other than one who engages in the study of Torah,"
וְשָׁנִינוּ (בְּפֶרֶק ג דְּאָבוֹת מִשְׁנָה ה): "כָּל הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֹל תּוֹרָה מַעֲבִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ עֹל מַלְכוּת וְעֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
". and we learned (in Avot 3:5): "Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah, they remove from him the yoke of government and the yoke of worldly care."
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה מְזַכֵּךְ בְּשַׂר הַגּוּף בְּיוֹתֵר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּסוֹף חֲגִיגָה כז
.): For the Torah refines and purifies the flesh of the body to the highest degree, as they stated (at the end of Chagigah 27a): "
תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁכָּל גּוּפָן אֵשׁ וְכוּלֵי", וְהוּא אֵשׁ שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה שֶׁאוֹכֶלֶת אֵשׁ, עַיֵּין שָׁם בַּתּוֹסָפוֹת דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל שֶׁאֵין (וּבְיוֹמָא כא
:), "Torah scholars, whose entire body is fire, etc.," which is the supernal fire that consumes lower fire, see Tosafot there s.v. She-ein (and in Yoma 21b),
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר דְּעַל כֵּן שׂוֹרֶפֶת אֵשׁ דְּגֵיהִנָּם וְאֵשׁ דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן אֵשׁ
, meaning that the fire of Torah consumes both the fire of Gehenna and the fire of the evil inclination, which is likewise fire,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּקִדּוּשִׁין פא.): "חֲזִי דְּאַתְּ נוּרָא וְכוּלֵי
", as they stated (in Kiddushin 81a): "See that you are fire and sins are tow, etc.," (
וּבְיוֹמָא סט:) "נְפַק אֲתָא כִּי גּוּרְיָא דְּנוּרָא וְכוּלֵי
", (and in Yoma 69b): "The inclination for idolatry emerged from the Holy of Holies like a fiery lion cub, etc.," (
וּבְהוֹשֵׁעַ ז, ו-ז) "כְּמוֹ תַנּוּר בֹּעֵרָה מֵאֹפֶה וְגוֹמֵר בֹּעֵר כְּאֵשׁ לֶהָבָה
" (and in Hosea 7:6-7): "They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker... burning like a flaming fire" (
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת ח עַמּוּד א: "תְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מִינֵי מִיתָה נִבְרְאוּ בָּעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם
, (and this corresponds to what they stated in Berakhot 8a: "Nine hundred and three [
תתק"ג
= 903] varieties of death were created in the world," see there,
בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים: קִנְאָה תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד שֶׁמּוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הָעוֹלָם, כִּדְתְנַן סוֹף פֶּרֶק ד דְּאָבוֹת [תתק"ג = ג' פְּעָמִים ש"א = אֵ"שׁ
]). which numerically equals three times 301 [
אֵשׁ
= 301], corresponding to the three fiery forces—envy, lust, and honor—that drive a person out of the world, as we learned at the end of the fourth chapter of Avot).

p: וְהֵם גַּם כֵּן שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם פֶּרֶק ב מִשְׁנָה יא): "עַיִן הָרָע וְיֵצֶר הָרָע וְשִׂנְאַת הַבְּרִיּוֹת מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הָעוֹלָם
". And these three are identical to the three things taught earlier (Avot 2:11): "An evil eye, the evil inclination, and hatred of fellow creatures drive a person out of the world." "
יֵצֶר הָרָע" סְתָם הוּא בְּתַאֲווֹת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל: "וְכָל יֵצֶר מַחְשְׁבֹת לִבּוֹ רַק רַע כָּל הַיּוֹם" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ו, ה

), For "the evil inclination" (yetzer hara) mentioned without qualification refers to bodily lust (ta'avah), as written regarding the Generation of the Flood: "And every inclination (yetzer) of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the day" (Genesis 6:5),
וּבְפָרָשַׁת נֹחַ: "כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו" (שָׁם ח, כא
). and in Parashat Noach: "For the inclination (yetzer) of man's heart is evil from his youth" (Genesis 8:21).
וְ"עַיִן הָרָע" בָּא מִקִּנְאָה
, An "evil eye" stems from envy (kin'ah),
וְ"שִׂנְאָה" מֵרְדִיפַת הַכָּבוֹד, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "גֶּבֶר יָהִיר וְלֹא יִנְוֶה" (חֲבַקּוּק ב, ה
) – and "hatred of fellow creatures" stems from the pursuit of honor and arrogance (kavod), as it is written: "A haughty man cannot abide at peace" (Habakkuk 2:5) –
אֲפִילּוּ אַאִינָשֵׁי בֵּיתֵיהּ לָא מִיקַּבֵּל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא צח.), וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹבְלוֹ
. meaning he is unacceptable even to the members of his own household, as they stated (in Bava Batra 98a), because no one can tolerate an arrogant person.
וְלִשְׁלָשְׁתָּם הָיָה הֲסָתַת הַנָּחָשׁ
: And the primordial serpent's incitement encompassed all three:
אַף שֶׁעִיקָּרוֹ בְּתַאֲוָה, הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הֲסָתַת כָּבוֹד – "וִהְיִיתֶם כֵּאלֹהִים" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, ה
), for even though his primary seduction was through lust, he enticed Eve through the allure of honor and haughtiness—"and you shall be like God" (Genesis 3:5),
וְזֶהוּ סוֹף הַגֵּיאוּת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר: "אֶעֱלֶה עַל בָּמֳתֵי עָב אֶדַּמֶּה לְעֶלְיוֹן" (יְשַׁעְיָה יד, יד
), which is the ultimate extreme of arrogance, just as Nebuchadnezzar boasted: "I will ascend above the heights of the clouds, I will make myself like the Most High" (Isaiah 14:14),
וְכֵן בְּחִירָם מֶלֶךְ צוֹר אָמַר: "אֵל אָנִי מוֹשַׁב אֱלֹהִים יָשַׁבְתִּי" (יְחֶזְקֵאל כח, ב
). and similarly Hiram, king of Tyre, declared: "I am a god, I sit in the seat of God" (Ezekiel 28:2).

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 23:13: “Rabbi Avin said: Four kinds of proud beings were created in the world: the proudest among creatures is man; the proudest among birds is the eagle; the proudest among domestic animals is the ox; the proudest among wild animals is the lion. Why all this? So that they should not become proud in the world, and should know that the kingdom of Heaven is over them. reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: Rava would regularly say: The goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, so that a person should not read Scripture and study Mishnah yet rebel against his father, his mother, his teacher, or someone greater than he in wisdom and number, as it says: “The beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem; good understanding belongs to all who practice them.” It does not say “to those who act,” but “to those who practice them”—to those who act for its own sake, and not to those who act for an ulterior purpose. Anyone who acts for an ulterior purpose would have been better off not being created.

paragraphs.text:
Taanit 7a:15-16: “And Rabbi Ḥanina bar Idi said: Why are matters of Torah likened to water, as it is written: “Ho, everyone who thirsts, come for water” (Isaiah 55:1)? This verse comes to tell you: Just as water leaves a high place and flows to a low place, so too, Torah matters are retained only by one whose spirit is lowly, i.e., a humble person.

And Rabbi Oshaya said: Why are matters of Torah likened to these three liquids: To water, wine and milk? As it is written with regard to water: “Ho, everyone who thirsts, come for water,” and it is written in the same verse: “Come, buy and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.” This verse comes to tell you: Just as these three liquids can be retained only in the least of vessels, e.g., clay pots, but not vessels of silver and gold, as they will spoil, so too, matters of Torah are retained only by one whose spirit is lowly.”

paragraphs.text: Orchot Tzadikim 1:36: “Pride in the attainment of wisdom is praiseworthy, as it says (Yirmiyahu 9:23), “Only in this should one who boasts boast: understanding and knowing Me.” He should increase his thanks to the Creator, blessed be He, and also knowledge, understanding, and good character, through prayer, saying, “I thank You for having placed my portion among those who sit in the beis midrash, and not among those who sit idly at street corners,” and likewise, “Fortunate are we: how good is our portion, and how pleasant our lot.” Concerning this it says (II Divrei HaYamim 17:6), “His heart was exalted in the ways of Hashem.” A person should possess a noble spirit and an aspiring heart in matters of the World to Come, so that he is not satisfied with whatever comes his way and does not say that the amount he has attained is enough. Rather, all his deeds should seem little in his eyes, his soul should continually aspire higher, and he should take himself to task as one falling short in the service of the Creator, blessed be He. This pride does not harm humility; rather, it assists it, leading him to rejoice in good qualities, to rejoice in the honor of his fellows, and to care for their honor.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: הַגַּאֲוָה בְּמַעֲלַת הַחָכְמָה מְשֻׁבַּחַת שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ירמיהו ט כג): ״כִּי אִם בְּזֹאת יִתְהַלֵּל הַמִּתְהַלֵּל: הַשְׂכֵּל וְיָדוֹעַ אוֹתִי״. וְיוֹסִיף הוֹדָאָה לַבּוֹרֵא בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְגַם דֵּעָה וְהַשְׂכֵּל וּמִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת בִּתְפִלָּה לוֹמַר: ״מוֹדֶה אֲנִי לְפָנֶיךָ, שֶׁנָּתַתָּ חֶלְקִי מִיּוֹשְׁבֵי בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, וְלֹא מִיּוֹשְׁבֵי קְרָנוֹת.״ וּכְמוֹ: ״אַשְׁרֵינוּ מַה טּוֹב חֶלְקֵנוּ וּמַה נָּעִים גּוֹרָלֵנוּ.״ וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (דברי הימים ב יז ו): ״וַיִּגְבַּהּ לִבּוֹ בְּדַרְכֵי יְיָ״. כִּי יִהְיֶה אָדָם יְקַר רוּחַ וּגְבַהּ לֵב בְּעִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁלֹּא יַסְפִּיק לוֹ בַּמֶּה שֶׁיִּזְדַּמֵּן לוֹ, וְלֹא יֹאמַר דַּי בַּמֶּה שֶׁיִּמָּצֵא יָדוֹ מֵהֶם; אֶלָּא יִמְעַט בְּעֵינָיו כָּל מַעֲשֵׂהוּ, וְתִגְבַּהּ נַפְשׁוֹ לְמַעְלָה תָּמִיד, וְיִתְרַעֵם בְּנַפְשׁוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּקַצֵּר מֵעֲבוֹדַת הַבּוֹרֵא בָּרוּךְ הוּא. וְזֹאת הַגַּאֲוָה אֵינָהּ מַזֶּקֶת לָעֲנָוָה אַךְ מְסַיַּעְתּוֹ, וְגוֹרֶמֶת לוֹ לִשְׂמֹחַ בַּמַּעֲלוֹת הַטּוֹבוֹת, וְלִשְׂמֹחַ בִּכְבוֹד חֲבֵרָיו וְלָחוּס עַל כְּבוֹדָם.
reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: Pride in the attainment of wisdom is praiseworthy, as it says (Yirmiyahu 9:23), “Only in this should one who boasts boast: understanding and knowing Me.” He should increase his thanks to the Creator, blessed be He, and also knowledge, understanding, and good character, through prayer, saying, “I thank You for having placed my portion among those who sit in the beis midrash, and not among those who sit idly at street corners,” and likewise, “Fortunate are we: how good is our portion, and how pleasant our lot.” Concerning this it says (II Divrei HaYamim 17:6), “His heart was exalted in the ways of Hashem.” A person should possess a noble spirit and an aspiring heart in matters of the World to Come, so that he is not satisfied with whatever comes his way and does not say that the amount he has attained is enough. Rather, all his deeds should seem little in his eyes, his soul should continually aspire higher, and he should take himself to task as one falling short in the service of the Creator, blessed be He. This pride does not harm humility; rather, it assists it, leading him to rejoice in good qualities, to rejoice in the honor of his fellows, and to care for their honor.

p: וְזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁלּוֹמֵד לִשְׁמָהּ עִם יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם, דְּזוּלַת זֶה נִקְרָא רַק "מְחִיר בְּיַד כְּסִיל וְגוֹמֵר", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּיוֹמָא עב:), עַיֵּין שָׁם

, However, this holds true only when one studies Torah for its own sake (lishmah) accompanied by fear of Heaven; otherwise, it is termed merely "a purchase price in the hand of a fool, when there is no heart," as they stated (in Yoma 72b), see there, (
וּבְשַׁבָּת לא סוֹף עַמּוּד א): "מוּטָב אִם לֹא הֶעֱלִיתָ", וְשָׁם רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב: "בְּהִי עָיֵיל

", (and in Shabbat 31a end): "If a person has grain (Torah) without preservative salt (fear of Heaven), it would have been better had he not brought it up to the loft," and at the top of 31b: "Through which doorway can one enter if he has the inner key without the outer key?"
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת יז.): "תַּכְלִית חָכְמָה תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא קוֹרֵא וְשׁוֹנֶה וּבוֹעֵט בְּאָבִיו וּבְרַבּוֹ וְכוּלֵי

". And this is what they taught (in Berakhot 17a): "The ultimate goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, so that a person should not read Scripture and study Mishnah and then kick against his father, his mother, and his teacher, etc."
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בַּמַּהֲרְשָׁ"א בְּחִידּוּשֵׁי אַגָּדוֹת הִקְשָׁה לָמָּה נָקַט זֶה דַּוְוקָא, יְעַיֵּין שָׁם
; See the Maharsha there in his Chiddushei Aggadot, who asks why Rava singled out kicking against one's parents and teacher specifically, see there;
אֲבָל פְּשׁוּטוֹ דְּהַכַּוָּנָה שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנֵס גֵּיאוּת בַּלֵּב עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
, yet the straightforward explanation is that the intention is that arrogance should not enter one's heart on account of his Torah knowledge, causing him to look down upon his elders—
דְּאַדְּרַבָּה, תַּכְלִית חָכְמָה תְּשׁוּבָה, דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מוֹדַעַת לֵיהּ חֲטָאוֹהִי
, for on the contrary, the true goal of wisdom is repentance, because the Torah makes a person acutely aware of his own failings and sins,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִשְׁבָּר וְנִשְׁפַּל לִבּוֹ בְּקִרְבּוֹ
. and through this his heart becomes broken and humbled within him.
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר: "כָּבוֹד חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ" (מִשְׁלֵי ג, לה
), Therefore it is stated: "The wise shall inherit honor" (Proverbs 3:35), (
וּבִנְדָרִים סב.) שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר אֶעֱשֶׂה מִצְוָה זוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיְּכַבְּדוּנִי, וְסוֹף הַכָּבוֹד לָבוֹא
, (and in Nedarim 62a) that one should not study in order to be called Rabbi, yet in the end honor will come of itself,
וְאֵין כָּבוֹד בָּא אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁבּוֹרֵחַ מִמֶּנּוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּעֵירוּבִין יג
:). for true honor comes only to one who flees from it, as they taught (in Eruvin 13b).
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמוֹ, הָיָה עָנָו מִכָּל הָאָדָם
, Indeed, Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who is the root of the Torah—which is called by his name ("Remember the Torah of Moses My servant")—was the humblest of all men (Numbers 12:3),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּחוּלִּין פט.) עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי אַתֶּם הַמְעַט מִכָּל הָעַמִּים" (דְּבָרִים ז, ז
): and as they stated (in Chullin 89a) on the verse "For you are the smallest of all the peoples" (Deuteronomy 7:7): "
כָּל שֶׁאֲנִי מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָכֶם גְּדוּלָּה אַתֶּם מְמַעֲטִין עַצְמְכֶם
", "Whenever I bestow greatness upon you, you humble yourselves before Me,"
וְהַיְינוּ כָּל מַה שֶּׁמּוֹסִיפִין הַשָּׂגַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ תּוֹסְפוֹת טוֹבָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
. meaning that the more they increase their comprehension of words of Torah—which is the true increase of goodness in Israel—the humbler they become. (
וּבְתַעֲנִית ז סוֹף עַמּוּד א) דְּאֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִתְקַיְּימִין אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁדַּעְתּוֹ שְׁפָלָה
, (And in Ta'anit 7a end) it is taught that words of Torah endure only in one whose mind is lowly and humble,
וְהַלּוֹמֵד לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם מֵבִיא הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שִׁפְלוּת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
. for when one studies for the sake of Heaven, the words of Torah themselves instill humility within him, as explained above.
וְגַם עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִתְקָן אוֹתוֹ מְעַט גֵּיאוּת שֶׁבַּבְּרִיאָה שֶׁהִיא לְצוֹרֶךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיִּגְבַּהּ לִבּוֹ בְּדַרְכֵי ה'" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב יז, ו

), Moreover, through words of Torah, that small measure of pride implanted in creation for a constructive purpose is rectified and elevated, as it is written: "And his heart was lifted up in the ways of Hashem" (II Chronicles 17:6),
וְאָמְרוּ (בְּסוֹטָה ה סוֹף עַמּוּד א): "תַּלְמִיד חָכָם צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ שְׁמִינִית שֶׁבִּשְׁמִינִית גַּאֲוָה", יְעַיֵּין שָׁם
, and as they taught (in Sotah 5a end): "A Torah scholar must possess one sixty-fourth (an eighth of an eighth) of pride," see there,
וְזֶהוּ הַתַּבְלִין שֶׁמְּתַבֵּל אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר מוּעָט שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ
. and this is how the Torah acts as a "spice" (tavlin)—seasoning and sanctifying that minute trace within him for the service of Heaven.

paragraphs.text: Pirkei Avot 5:19: “Whoever possesses these three things, he is of the disciples of Abraham, our father; and [whoever possesses] three other things, he is of the disciples of Balaam, the wicked. A good eye, a humble spirit and a moderate appetite he is of the disciples of Abraham, our father. An evil eye, a haughty spirit and a limitless appetite he is of the disciples of Balaam, the wicked. What is the difference between the disciples of Abraham, our father, and the disciples of Balaam, the wicked? The disciples of Abraham, our father, enjoy this world, and inherit the world to come, as it is said: “I will endow those who love me with substance, I will fill their treasuries” (Proverbs 8:21). But the disciples of Balaam, the wicked, inherit Gehinnom, and descend into the nethermost pit, as it is said: “For you, O God, will bring them down to the nethermost pit those murderous and treacherous men; they shall not live out half their days; but I trust in You” (Psalms 55:24).”

p: וְאֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשׁ קְלִיפּוֹת הֵם נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
: Now these three impure husks (envy, lust, and honor) stand opposite the three Patriarchs in the realm of holiness:
אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מַכְנִיס כָּל אֲהָבוֹת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, וְיִצְחָק הַגְּבוּרוֹת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
; Abraham our father, peace be upon him, brings all loves and desires into holiness (Chesed, on the right), and Isaac brings all severities and restraints into holiness (Gevurah, on the left);
וְ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה", הָעוֹמֵד נֶגֶד חֲבֵירוֹ יְמִינוֹ נֶגֶד שְׂמֹאלוֹ, וְעַל כֵּן גַּם קִנְאָה קוֹדֵם תַּאֲוָה

; and since God made "one opposite the other" (Ecclesiastes 7:14), when one stands facing his counterpart, his right faces the other's left—which is why in the Mishnah "envy" (stemming from the unrectified left/severity, facing Abraham's right) is listed before "lust" (stemming from the unrectified right/desire, facing Isaac's left);
וְכָבוֹד נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב הַקָּטָן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "קָטֹנְתִּי מִכֹּל הַחֲסָדִים" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לב, יא
), while the pursuit of "honor" stands opposite Jacob the small, as it is written: "I am too small for all the kindnesses" (Genesis 32:11),
וְנֶאֱמַר (עָמוֹס ז, ב): "מִי יָקוּם יַעֲקֹב כִּי קָטֹן הוּא
". and it is stated (Amos 7:2): "How shall Jacob stand, for he is small!"
וְהֵם נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה יְסוֹדוֹת אמ"ש (אֵשׁ, מַיִם, רוּחַ
): And they also correspond to the three primordial elements—Alef (Air/Spirit), Mem (Water), and Shin (Fire)—of Sefer Yetzirah:
וְגַסּוּת הָרוּחַ הוּא מִיסוֹד הָרוּחַ, "רוּחַ גְּבוֹהָה", וְהֵם שְׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת דְּבִלְעָם הָרָשָׁע (שֶׁבְּפֶרֶק ה דְּאָבוֹת מִשְׁנָה יט
), arrogance of spirit (gasut ha-ruach) stems from the element of Air/Spirit—a "haughty spirit" (ruach gevohah), which is one of the three traits of the wicked Balaam (in Avot 5:19)—
וְרוֹצֶה לִהְיוֹת עוֹלֶה לְמַעְלָה מַעְלָה כְּטֶבַע יְסוֹד הָאֵשׁ
, seeking to rise ever upward like the nature of the element of Fire;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה הוּא "רוּחַ נְמוּכָה
", whereas in holiness, the trait of the disciples of Abraham is a "lowly spirit" (ruach nemukhah).
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִיצּוֹל גַּם כֵּן מִתַּאֲוָה, שֶׁהוּא נִקְרָא בַּמִּשְׁנָה שָׁם "נֶפֶשׁ שְׁפָלָה" נֶגֶד "נֶפֶשׁ רְחָבָה" דְּבִלְעָם

. And through this humility one is also saved from lust, which is called in the Mishnah there a "humble soul" (nefesh shefalah) in contrast to the "greedy, expansive soul" (nefesh rechavah) of Balaam.
וְיֵצֶר דְּתַאֲוָה גַּם כֵּן אֵשׁ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, אַף שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה הוּא מַיִם שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ אֵשׁ
, Now the inclination of lust in the realm of impurity is a burning fire as noted above, even though its root in holiness (Chesed / love) corresponds to Water, which is the opposite of fire;
אֲבָל מָצִינוּ גַּם בִּקְדוּשָּׁה: "מַיִם רַבִּים לֹא יוּכְלוּ לְכַבּוֹת אֶת הָאַהֲבָה וְגוֹמֵר" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ח, ז), שֶׁבּוֹעֵר כָּאֵשׁ לְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
. yet we find in the realm of holiness as well: "Many waters cannot quench the love, for its flashes are flashes of fire" (Song of Songs 8:6-7), burning like fire with love for Hashem, blessed be He.
עַד כָּאן מִכְּתַב יַד קֹדֶשׁ
. Thus far from the holy manuscript.
